body_text:
¶ Plywood Cutting Troubleshooting
¶ Overview
Laser cutting plywood involves many variables, including material quality, adhesive composition, laser settings, optical condition, and machine maintenance. Even with the correct machine setup, inconsistent plywood or worn components can lead to cutting defects.
This guide lists the most common problems encountered when laser cutting plywood, their possible causes, and recommended corrective actions.
Tip
Before adjusting machine parameters, verify that the plywood is suitable for laser processing. Refer to Plywood Selection Guide for material recommendations.
¶ Problem 1: The Plywood Does Not Cut Through
¶ Possible Causes
Laser power is too low.
Cutting speed is too high.
The laser is out of focus.
The plywood is thicker than the machine's cutting capability.
Poor-quality plywood contains thick adhesive layers or internal voids.
The lens or mirrors are contaminated.
The laser beam is misaligned.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Increase laser power gradually.
Reduce cutting speed in small increments.
Verify and adjust the focus position.
Perform multiple cutting passes instead of using excessive power.
Clean the optical components.
Check beam alignment according to the machine maintenance procedure.
Test a different sheet of plywood to rule out material defects.
¶ Problem 2: The Cut Edges Are Excessively Burned
¶ Possible Causes
Cutting speed is too slow.
Laser power is unnecessarily high.
Air Assist airflow is insufficient.
Smoke is trapped inside the kerf.
The plywood contains excessive resin or adhesive.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Increase cutting speed while maintaining complete penetration.
Reduce laser power if possible.
Verify that Air Assist is functioning properly.
Clean the exhaust system to improve smoke removal.
Use higher-quality laser-grade plywood.
¶ Problem 3: Heavy Smoke Is Produced During Cutting
¶ Possible Causes
Inadequate exhaust ventilation.
Insufficient Air Assist.
High moisture content in the plywood.
Adhesive or resin-rich plywood.
Dirty cutting table restricting airflow.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Check that the exhaust fan is operating correctly.
Increase airflow if the machine allows adjustment.
Dry or properly store plywood before use.
Remove accumulated debris beneath the workpiece.
Replace poor-quality plywood if excessive smoke persists.
¶ Problem 4: Flames Appear During Cutting
Small, short-lived flames are common when cutting wood. However, sustained flames indicate that the material is burning instead of being efficiently removed.
¶ Possible Causes
Air Assist is disabled or insufficient.
Cutting speed is too slow.
Resin-rich plywood ignites easily.
Smoke accumulates around the cutting area.
Combustible debris is present on the worktable.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Confirm that Air Assist is enabled.
Increase cutting speed where appropriate.
Clean the honeycomb or blade table before processing.
Improve exhaust airflow.
Never leave the machine unattended while cutting wood.
Warning
If flames continue for more than a few seconds or spread beyond the cutting path, stop the job immediately and inspect the machine before continuing.
¶ Problem 5: The Bottom Edge Is Not Completely Cut
¶ Possible Causes
Focus position is incorrect.
Material thickness exceeds the laser's capability.
Insufficient laser power reaches the bottom of the kerf.
Smoke blocks the laser beam inside the cut.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Adjust the focal position slightly below the material surface when appropriate.
Reduce cutting speed.
Perform an additional cutting pass.
Verify that the lens is clean.
Increase Air Assist to clear debris from the kerf.
¶ Problem 6: The Kerf Is Wider Than Expected
¶ Possible Causes
Laser focus is incorrect.
Lens contamination reduces beam quality.
Cutting speed is too slow.
The selected lens is unsuitable for the material thickness.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Recheck the focus distance.
Clean the lens and mirrors.
Increase cutting speed if excessive heat is causing edge widening.
Verify that the correct focal length lens is installed.
¶ Problem 7: Engraving Appears Uneven
¶ Possible Causes
Natural variations in wood grain.
Uneven plywood density.
Warped material.
Dirty optics.
Inconsistent engraving speed.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Secure the plywood so it remains flat.
Clean optical components.
Use consistent engraving settings.
Perform engraving tests on scrap material before production.
Keep in mind that wood is a natural material, and slight variations in engraving appearance are normal.
¶ Problem 8: Smoke Residue Covers the Surface
¶ Possible Causes
Weak exhaust airflow.
Dirty honeycomb table.
Insufficient Air Assist.
Protective masking was not used when appropriate.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Improve exhaust performance.
Clean the worktable regularly.
Increase Air Assist during cutting.
Apply removable masking tape to finished surfaces when appearance is critical.
Wipe the surface with an appropriate cleaner after processing.
¶ Problem 9: The Lens Becomes Dirty Quickly
¶ Possible Causes
Excessive smoke production.
Poor-quality plywood adhesives.
Weak exhaust performance.
Airflow around the lens is insufficient.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Clean the lens according to the recommended maintenance schedule.
Improve smoke extraction.
Use higher-quality plywood with cleaner adhesive layers.
Inspect the Air Assist nozzle for blockages.
Dirty optics reduce laser power and may eventually cause permanent lens damage if not cleaned regularly.
¶ Problem 10: The Plywood Is Warped After Cutting
¶ Possible Causes
Excessive heat accumulation.
High moisture content.
Uneven material quality.
Improper storage before processing.
¶ Recommended Solutions
Store plywood flat in a dry environment.
Use optimized cutting parameters to minimize heat input.
Reduce unnecessary laser dwell time.
Select higher-quality plywood with better dimensional stability.
¶ Quick Troubleshooting Checklist
Before making major parameter adjustments, verify the following:
Is the plywood suitable for laser cutting?
Is the material flat and dry?
Is the laser correctly focused?
Are the lens and mirrors clean?
Is Air Assist operating normally?
Is the exhaust system removing smoke effectively?
Are the power and speed settings appropriate?
Has a test cut been performed on this batch of plywood?
Following this checklist can resolve many common cutting issues without extensive machine adjustments.
¶ Summary
Most plywood cutting problems result from a combination of material quality, laser settings, airflow, and machine maintenance rather than a single cause. Systematically checking each factor helps identify the source of the problem quickly and reduces unnecessary adjustments.
Maintaining clean optics, using quality plywood, optimizing cutting parameters, and ensuring proper ventilation are the most effective ways to achieve consistent cutting performance.
¶ See Also
Plywood Selection Guide
Plywood Laser Cutting Best Practices
Air Assist Guide
Laser Focus Adjustment Guide
Optics Cleaning and Maintenance Guide
¶ Frequently Asked Questions
¶ Why does one sheet of plywood cut differently from another?
Even plywood with the same thickness may differ in wood species, adhesive formulation, moisture content, and internal construction. These variations affect cutting performance and often require parameter adjustments.
¶ Can poor plywood damage my laser machine?
Poor-quality plywood can generate excessive smoke and adhesive residue, contaminating the lens, mirrors, and exhaust system. While it may not immediately damage the machine, it increases maintenance requirements and can reduce cutting performance over time.
¶ Why does the laser cut through one side but not the other?
This is often caused by warped material, inconsistent plywood density, internal voids, incorrect focus, or beam misalignment.
¶ What should I check first when cutting quality suddenly decreases?
Start with the basics: inspect the lens and mirrors, verify the focus, confirm that Air Assist and the exhaust system are functioning correctly, and perform a small test cut before changing power or speed settings.

title: Fix Hazy or Blurry Laser Camera Lens Surface
excerpt: An integrated workspace camera is an incredible tool for visual alignment, but it only works if it can see clearly. If your video feed has become cloudy, milky, or out of focus, it
body_text:
¶ Hazy or Smudged Camera Lens Surface - Hydra Series
An integrated workspace camera is an incredible tool for visual alignment, but it only works if it can see clearly. If your video feed has become cloudy, milky, or out of focus, it will prevent you from properly placing your graphics. This guide walks you through the causes of camera haze—from organic smoke buildup to interior condensation—and how to fix the image feed.
¶ Problem Description
A hazy, cloudy layer of residue or grime forms on the surface of the camera lens. When opening the camera inside LightBurn, the image appears blurry, making alignment and software utilization impossible.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
Haze on the Exterior Lens Surface: Long-term cutting or engraving of organic materials (such as wood or acrylic) releases wood tars, resins, and various chemical byproducts. These airborne particles condense over time on the exposed outer glass of the camera, building up a stubborn, cloudy film.
Haze on the Interior Lens Surface: If the working environment is cold, or if the camera was previously disassembled and lost its airtight seal, ambient moisture and fine airborne dust can penetrate inside the camera module, creating a hazy condensation layer on the inner lens surface.
¶ Solution
¶ Step 1. Clean the Lens with a Specialized Lens Cleaner
Use a dedicated optical lens cleaning solution paired with an ultra-fine microfiber cloth (or pre-moistened optical lens wipes) to gently wipe down the outer surface of camera.
¶ Step 2. Replace the Camera Module
If the image feed remains blurry after thoroughly cleaning the exterior lens as described in Step 1, it indicates that the contamination or moisture film is trapped on the inside of the camera module.
Note: Attempting to crack open the camera housing will permanently break its factory environmental seal and introduce airborne dust. Furthermore, the camera will require complete recalibration after any teardown. Please contact ONELASER After-Sales Support to secure a replacement camera module assembly.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Auto-Focus Failure Troubleshooting Guide - X Series
excerpt: Auto-focus failure is usually caused by a jammed or damaged sensor, incorrect Z-axis settings, or faulty limit switches. Most issues can be resolved by cleaning the sensor, checkin
body_text:
¶ Auto-focus Failure - X Series
Auto-focus failure is usually caused by a jammed or damaged sensor, incorrect Z-axis settings, or faulty limit switches. Most issues can be resolved by cleaning the sensor, checking LightBurn Z-axis parameters, and verifying limit switch status before requiring hardware replacement.
¶ Problem Description
When auto-focus is initiated, the laser head moves upward until it stalls at the highest position.
When auto-focus is initiated, the laser head moves downward, contacts the material, but continues to attempt to move down without stopping.
When auto-focus is initiated, the laser head has no reaction.
¶ Cause
The auto-focus sensor may be stuck or jammed by debris or grease generated during processing.
The sensor may be burnt out or damaged due to high temperatures during processing.
The Z-axis limit switch is damaged.
The parameter settings for the Z-axis are incorrect.
The lead screw of the Z-axis motor is bent, causing the moving component riding along the threads to bind or jam at that specific location, which prevents downward autofocus and Z-axis motion.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Check Z-Axis Settings in Machine Parameters
Check the Machine Settings in your software (e.g. LightBurn).
In the Z axis settings section, check if the Limit Trigger is disabled. If it is, re-enable it.
¶ Method 2. Check if the Auto-Focus Sensor is Stuck or Jammed
If the light inside the sensor is red, it means the sensor is constantly triggered. This will cause the Z-axis to keep moving up until it stalls at the maximum height.
Gently press the nozzle by hand to ensure it is retractable (it contains a spring structure).
Regularly clean the nozzle and sensor to prevent debris and grease from jamming the sensor:
Turn off the machine.
Unscrew the sensor's securing screws.
Use alcohol and a cotton swab to clean the interior.
Reassemble and secure the components.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Method 3. Check for Burnt Sensor or Wiring
Open the laser head box. Inspect the auto-focus sensor and its connecting wires for any signs of melting, shorting, burning, or breakage.
¶ Method 4. Check Limit Switches and Sensor Status
If you cannot visually determine if the limit switch or sensor is faulty, open the Diagnose page on the controller or software.
Manually press the laser nozzle or the sensor, and the Z-axis upper limit switch.
Observe whether the corresponding Z- and Z+ buttons on the Diagnose page change from green to red. If there is no change, the switch or sensor may be damaged.
¶ Method 5. Check the Spring Status Inside the Autofocus Component
Move the laser head upward along the Z-axis. After unscrewing the nozzle, you will be able to see the screws at the bottom of the laser head.
Once these screws are removed, take out the autofocus component and inspect the internal spring. Check whether it has lost its elasticity or become misaligned, which can prevent the autofocus sensor from springing back and cause the function to fail.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Method 6. Inspect the Z-Axis Lead Screw Motor
Power OFF the machine and manually rotate the Z-axis motor lead screw by hand and feel for any sudden resistance, binding, or tight spots. If you feel a noticeable physical jam or constraint, please contact ONELASER After-Sales Support to arrange for a replacement Z-axis lead screw motor.
Important Note: Do not attempt to use tools or external physical force to bend the lead screw back straight yourself, which will cause secondary structural damage.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Fix Stray Fragmented Lines Around Laser Engraving
excerpt: When random, scattered lines or small artifacts appear around the perimeter of an engraved design, it can ruin an otherwise perfect project. Because the original file looks clean a
body_text:
¶ Stray Fragmented Lines Appear Around Engraved Graphics - VertiGO Series
When random, scattered lines or small artifacts appear around the perimeter of an engraved design, it can ruin an otherwise perfect project. Because the original file looks clean and may even process flawlessly on other machines, this issue points to a localized hardware vibration or data transfer error. This guide walks you through stabilizing your optical path and fixing data corruption to restore crisp, clean engraving edges.
¶ Problem Description
Small, scattered, fragmented short lines appear around the perimeter of the engraved design that are completely absent from the original project file. Processing the exact same file on other laser machines yields perfect results with no artifacts.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
The processing file data package becomes corrupted or suffers from package loss while being sent to the laser motherboard.
One or more lenses or mirrors along the optical path are loose, vibrating under the physical inertial forces of the laser head's movement and throwing off the beam trajectory.
¶ Solution
¶ Step 1. Modify the File Transfer Method or Connection Protocol
1. If you typically click "Start" directly inside your laser software to process jobs on the fly, data packet loss can occur during transmitting. Instead, click "Send" to upload the entire project file directly into the laser controller's onboard memory first. Once the transfer is complete, press "Start" on the machine's physical control panel to run the job locally.
2. You could try changing your connection method, as your current connection might be affected by something, such as external electromagnetic interference.
USB Connection
Ethernet Connection
Wi-Fi Connection
¶ Step 2. Inspect the Entire Optical Path for Loose Optics
Starting directly from where the laser beam exits the RF tube, check the following components for any physical play or looseness: Beam Expander, 1st Mirror, Beam Combiner, 2nd Mirror, 3rd Mirror, and the Focus Lens.
If any lens or mirror is loose within its retaining housing, the rapid acceleration and deceleration of the laser head during engraving will cause that optic to shake. As the laser beam passes through a vibrating optic, its exit angle shifts dynamically, striking the material incorrectly and creating unintended stray lines.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Fix Laser Head Crashing with Cross-Hatch Enabled
excerpt: If your laser machine makes a loud crashing sound or engraves completely outside your design bounds whenever you enable Cross-Hatch or change the Scan Angle, you are experiencing a
body_text:
¶ Laser Head Collisions and Errors with Cross-Hatch Engraving Enabled
If your laser machine makes a loud crashing sound or engraves completely outside your design bounds whenever you enable Cross-Hatch or change the Scan Angle, you are experiencing an axis inertia overload. This guide explains why gantry-style lasers struggle with multi-directional scanning and provides safe alternative workflows to achieve the same textured engraving effects without damaging your hardware.
¶ Problem Description
When engraving with the Cross-Hatch feature enabled or a custom Scan Angle configured, the laser head moves along the Y-axis (or at a diagonal angle). During this process, the machine emits a loud mechanical crashing sound, and engraves outside the bounds of the actual design.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
Due to the physical design of gantry-style laser systems, the Y-axis motor carries significantly more weight than the X-axis motor. Mechanically, this extra mass prevents the Y-axis from sustaining long-term, high-frequency directional changes at high speeds.
Enabling the Cross-Hatch function (or modifying the scanning angle) forces the heavy Y-axis to jog back and forth at high speeds, or compels both the X and Y axes to execute rapid, alternating reciprocating movements simultaneously. This leads to lost steps and collisions.
⚠️ Hardware Warning: We strongly advise against using the Cross-Hatch function on gantry-style machines to prevent premature hardware wear.
¶ Solution: How to Safely Achieve Multidirectional Engraving Effects
¶ Method 1. Rotate the Graphic or the Material (Recommended)
Rotate the design or physical material while keeping the machine's underlying Scan Angle at 0°. For example, if you want a 45° engraving effect, select the graphic inside LightBurn and use the rotation tool to spin it 45° on the canvas (or physically rotate your raw material by 45° on the honeybed).
This workflow entirely bypasses stressful Y-axis reciprocal shaking, protects your hardware from damage, and yields the fastest possible processing times.
¶ Method 2. Substantially Lower the Processing Speed
If your workflow absolutely requires the use of LightBurn's Cross-Hatch or angled scanning parameters, you must downscale your speed to compensate for the axis inertia.
Although the factory Machine Settings may list the maximum Y-axis speed at 300mm/s, the axis cannot safely sustain continuous directional reversals at this speed. Lower your engraving speed to under 100mm/s. Exceeding 100mm/s will cause violent machine shaking.
Note: Even at lower speeds, prolonged use of this method accelerates the wear and tear of mechanical components like belts and linear bearings, and may lead to inconsistent engraving quality over time.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Fix Intermittent Laser Output At Low Power
excerpt: If your CO2 laser machine fires normally at high power but skips, pulses, or cuts out completely at lower power settings, you are dealing with a critical firing threshold issue. Th
body_text:
¶ Intermittent or Halting Laser Output at Low Power, Normal at High Power - XT Model
If your CO2 laser machine fires normally at high power but skips, pulses, or cuts out completely at lower power settings, you are dealing with a critical firing threshold issue. This troubleshooting guide addresses why your laser might halt or make a clicking noise at lower power settings (e.g., 20%) and provides clear steps to isolate the issue across your cooling loop, laser tube, and power supply.
¶ Problem Description
The machine fails to output a continuous laser beam at low power settings, emitting instead in sporadic pulses. Every time the laser cuts out or fires back up, a clicking sound can be heard. For example, at 20% power, the cutting process is highly intermittent and eventually halts completely before completing the job. However, when the power is set above 28%, both cutting and engraving operate perfectly normal.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
The cooling system's water level is low, or the flow/water sensor is malfunctioning.
The CO2 glass laser tube is leaking internal gas, degrading its ionization capability.
The power supply cannot maintain a stable striking voltage.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Inspect the Water Level and Sensor
¶ Step 1. Replenish the Water Chiller
Open the back panel of the machine to locate the cooling system. Look at the water level sensor. If the water is low, you will likely notice that the red light on the sensor is off. Add the water until the level reaches the bottom of the neck line. Once the water is at the correct level, check the sensor again to see if the red light has turned back on.
¶ Step 2. Bypass the Water Sensor for Testing
Turn off the machine and locate the TL-Timing board. Unplug the yellow-green wire indicated by the red arrow in the image. Then use a conductive material to short-circuit IN11 and GND on the board.
After shorting, check whether the laser fault still occurs when running a job. While the machine is running, check the water sensor status. If the status is unclear, record a video and contact the OneLaser customer service team for further assistance.
¶ Method 2. Observe the Glass Laser Tube Condition
Open the back cover of the machine. Ensuring you can safely and directly view the tube (wear appropriate laser safety goggles if available), run a low-power processing job and observe the physical reaction inside the glass tube:
Check the Color of the Ionized Gas inside the inner tube:
Normal (No Leaks): A vibrant, solid pink or pinkish-purple glow.
Abnormal (Gas Leak Present): A dull grayish-white, pale blue, or tinted greenish hue.
Severe Gas Depletion: The tube will only show a very faint, thin white electrical arc.
Check the Behavior of the Electrical Arc:
Normal: A perfectly straight, stable, and steady beam of light.
Abnormal: Intermittent flickering, jumping, or a twisted electrical path.
¶ Method 3. Check the Power Supply
Run a low-power processing task. While the job is running, use a multimeter to measure the 48V input terminal on the mainboard:
If the voltage stays stable at around 48V: The power supply is delivering adequate wattage, pointing to a failing glass laser tube.
If the voltage drops significantly below 48V or cuts out momentarily: The power supply unit itself is defective.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Fix Laser Offset Between Actual & Set Start Point
excerpt: This guide helps you diagnose and resolve instances where the actual laser processing point does not match your software's set starting point. By adjusting your software origins, h
body_text:
¶ Offset Between Actual and Set Starting Point - X Series
This guide helps you diagnose and resolve instances where the actual laser processing point does not match your software's set starting point. By adjusting your software origins, homing offsets, or red dot pointers, you can restore perfect precision to your machine.
¶ Problem Description
After setting the start position, the actual point where the laser begins processing does not align with the intended design starting point. This causes the engraved or cut graphics to shift from their expected position on the material.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
If the Start From mode is set to Absolute Coords:
It may be caused by a mismatch between the job origin, workarea origin, or start position settings. (See Method 1 for the fix)
It could be due to a physical misalignment between the software's coordinate origin and the machine's actual mechanical origin. (See Method 2 for the fix)
If the Start From mode is set to Current Position:
The variance is likely caused by a offset between the red dot pointer and the actual laser beam path. (See Method 3 for the fix)
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Verify Origin and Start Position Settings
Ensure that your graphic/job origin, the software Start From position, and the machine's zero point are all uniformally set to the Rear Left corner. Run a test job to see if the offset is resolved.
graphic/job origin
Start From position
machine's zero point
¶ Method 2. Adjust the Software Home Offset
¶ Step 1. Reboot or Reset the Device
Restart the machine or press the Reset button on the control panel to force the machine to home. This ensures the controller accurately recalculates its coordinate system and homing zero positions.
¶ Step 2. Calibrate the Home Offset
Set the Start From option to Absolute Coords in LightBurn. Draw a simple rectangle on the canvas and set its X and Y coordinates to (0,0) (positioning it exactly at the software origin), then run the job. Then measure the offset distance between where the rectangle actually fired and the physical zero point edge of your workspace grid.
Go to Machine Settings in LightBurn. Expand the X Axis Settings and Y Axis Settings menus respectively, locate the Home offset fields, and input the measured variance values to correct the alignment.
¶ Method 3. Calibrate the Red Dot Pointer Alignment
¶ Step 1. Configure the Laser Offset in Software
You can adjust the software offset compensation parameters by following the official LightBurn guide: LightBurn Laser Offset Setup
¶ Step 2. Manually Align the Red Dot Optical Path
Alternatively, you can physically adjust the red dot beam alignment by following this step-by-step FAQ troubleshooting guide: Red Dot Pointer Misalignment with Laser Beam - X Series
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: LightBurn 2.1.0 Device & Camera Fixes
excerpt: This guide explains how to troubleshoot device detection issues, camera calibration errors, unit setting changes, and machine parameter problems that may occur after upgrading to L
body_text:
¶ Device Info & Camera Errors After Upgrading to LightBurn 2.1.0
This guide explains how to troubleshoot device detection issues, camera calibration errors, unit setting changes, and machine parameter problems that may occur after upgrading to LightBurn 2.1.0. Follow the steps below to restore normal operation and ensure accurate processing performance.
¶ Problem Description
After upgrading LightBurn to version 2.1.0 and reopening the software, you may encounter the following issues:
Previously connected machines may disappear from the device list, requiring you to search for and add them again.
Factory machine configuration parameters inside the controller may change, leading to motion control errors or poor processing results.
The default control and design measurement units may toggle unexpectedly.
Incorrect selection or accidental swapping of laser tube types on a dual-source laser system.
Camera calibration files from older versions are automatically converted to a new format, which can introduce alignment errors or offsets.
¶ Cause
A software logic bug in the newly released LightBurn 2.1.0 update causes certain configuration files and user profiles to migrate incorrectly.
¶ Solution
¶ Step 1. Re-discover and Reconnect the Device
If your machine profile has disappeared from the device list in the bottom-right panel, click the "Find My Laser" or "Create Manually" button to rediscover and re-add your machine to restore communication.
¶ Step 2. Correct the Measurement and Control Units
If the machine exhibits control or processing issues (for example: setting the jog distance to 10mm, but the laser head actually moves 70mm), the unit system has likely been altered.
Click the Wrench icon (Device Settings) in the top toolbar. Locate the Control Units section and change it back to your original preference (typically mm/min or mm/sec).
Adjust the "Link Control and Design Units" toggle based on your workflow:
Toggle ON: Changing the machine's control units will automatically change your measurement units on the canvas toolbar as well.
Toggle OFF: The design units on your workspace canvas can be switched between mm and in independently without altering the machine's control units.
¶ Step 3. Re-import the Standard Vendor Parameters
Because internal controller settings may have changed, you need to flash the factory-fresh machine parameters:
Contact the ONELASER after-sales technical support team, state your machine model, and request the official standard factory parameters file.
Go to Machine Settings in LightBurn, click Load from File to import the file, and then click Write to save these settings directly to the motherboard.
Note: If you had any personalized or custom adjustments prior to the update, you will need to reconfigure them manually after writing the factory file.
¶ Step 4. Verify Laser Tube Type Configurations (Tube 1 / Tube 2)
After importing the standard factory parameter file, the laser tube types are generally calibrated automatically. However, to rule out any anomalies, you should manually double-check the configuration:
Scroll down to the Laser Settings section and locate Tube 1 Type and Tube 2 Type to confirm their classifications. Example: For the Hydra GEN1, Laser 1 should be configured as a Glass Tube, and Laser 2 should be configured as an RF Tube.
To verify which tube is mapped to each setting, navigate to Menu > Alignment on the machine's control panel. You can manually toggle between Laser 1 and Laser 2. Press the Pulse button to fire a test beam. Observe the hardware directly to see which laser tube fires during the pulse test for each selection.
¶ Step 5. Re-calibrate the Camera
This problem occurs more frequently on Mac systems
Upon launching version 2.1.0, LightBurn will display a pop-up warning stating that your camera configuration file is from an older version and will ask Do you want to convert and import it into the latest format?
Please click Yes to allow the software to import the file.
To eliminate any conversion drift, open the Camera Calibration wizards. Follow the on-screen step-by-step prompts using your original alignment pattern to recalibrate and ensure precision.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Laser Head Drifts Off Path During Motion
excerpt: This guide explains why the laser head may drift from its intended path during movement or operation, and provides step-by-step instructions to restore proper alignment and smooth
body_text:
¶ Laser Head Drifts from Normal Path During Moving - Hydra Series
This guide explains why the laser head may drift from its intended path during movement or operation, and provides step-by-step instructions to restore proper alignment and smooth motion.
¶ Problem Description
During moving and operation, the laser head drifts away from its intended path at certain locations. Once the job finishes, the laser head moves noticeably slower when traveling to the left, even makes a loud, grinding noise during homing.
When the machine is powered off, pushing the laser head manually reveals significant resistance, and the movement is not smooth.
¶ Cause
The laser head is secured to the X-axis guide rail via rollers. If the rollers derail from the guide track, movement becomes restricted, requiring the laser head assembly to be reseated. This derailment is typically caused by a prior head collision with the gantry frame or the autofocus mechanism pushing up too forcefully against a workpiece.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Solution
¶ Step 1. Loosen the Rollers and Reseat the Laser Head
Use a 2 mm hex wrench to unscrew the retaining screws located on the back of the two bottom rollers.
Once these screws are loosened, you should be able to manipulate all four rollers (top and bottom) and pop them back securely into the grooves of the guide rail.
Note: The top rollers are obscured by the belt mounting hardware, making them difficult to access.
¶ Step 2. Tighten the Cam Screws and Test
Once the laser head is perfectly squared up and all rollers are fully snapped back onto the guide rail, reinstall and firmly tighten the retaining screws.
Run a standard test to verify smooth motion and ensure the rollers do not slip off the track again.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Fix Tumbler Engraving Jitter & Missing Areas
excerpt: This guide explains how to diagnose and resolve edge jitter, inconsistent engraving quality, and missing sections when engraving tumblers, cups, or other cylindrical objects. These
body_text:
¶ Incomplete Engraving & Edge Jitter on Tumblers - VertiGO Series
This guide explains how to diagnose and resolve edge jitter, inconsistent engraving quality, and missing sections when engraving tumblers, cups, or other cylindrical objects. These issues are typically caused by incorrect scanning offset settings or loose optical components that affect laser beam stability.
¶ Problem Description
When engraving tumblers or cups, regardless of whether the cup is placed opening-up or opening-down, the engraved pattern exhibits noticeable jitter along the edges, and certain sections of the design fail to engrave entirely.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
The backlash parameters have either not been uploaded to the controller or contain inaccuracies.
Components along the optical path are loose, causing the laser beam to vibrate or drift during high-speed engraving.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Calibrate Scanning Offset Parameters
The process for tuning scanning offsets is universal across our systems. Please follow the step-by-step diagnostic guide found in this article: How to Adjust the Backlash Parameters
¶ Method 2. Inspect the Optical Path Mirrors and Lenses
The laser beam originates from the RF tube and travels through a series of optics.
You must inspect the 1st Mirror, 2nd Mirror and 3rd Mirror for any looseness.
Check the two black screws securing the focus lens carriage assembly and ensure they are tightly fastened.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Fix Servo Driver Er190 Error
excerpt: This guide explains how to diagnose and fix the Servo Driver Er190 error on ONELASER machines. If the laser head suddenly stops during processing and the servo driver displays the
body_text:
¶ Laser Head Stops Suddenly with Servo Driver Error Er190 - Hydra GEN2 Series
This guide explains how to diagnose and fix the Servo Driver Er190 error on ONELASER machines. If the laser head suddenly stops during processing and the servo driver displays the Er190 alarm, this article will help you identify whether the issue is caused by mechanical vibration, belt tension, loose structural components, or incorrect servo driver parameters.
¶ Problem Description
During processing, the laser head suddenly stops moving while running at low speeds. Upon inspecting the servo motor drivers inside the bottom-right door panel of the machine, the driver screen displays the error code Er190. Rebooting the equipment clears the error, but running the machine causes the driver to trigger the same error.
When the laser head moves along the X-axis and passes through a specific point, the belt vibrates violently at a very high frequency. Once the laser head moves past that specific point, the vibration stops immediately.
¶ Cause
According to the servo system manual, the Er190 error typically caused by:
Mechanical resonance.
Excessive current loop gain.
The current vibration threshold being set too low.
In the actual operating environment of this machine, the most probable cause is low-frequency mechanical vibration.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Check the Machine Hardware
¶ Step 1. Loosen the belt and test again
Slightly loosen the tension of the motion belt, then run a normal processing job to let the motor move. If the Er190 error does not reappear, it confirms that the root cause is mechanical tension/vibration rather than a fault inside the servo system itself.
¶ Step 2. Inspect the machine for loose structural parts
Check the entire machine for any loose components (including the machine casing, joints, and internal components). Focus heavily on the motion system—such as the belts, rails, gantry, and couplings—to ensure all components are properly tightened. Afterward, restart the machine and check if the error is resolved.
¶ Method 2. Modify Speed Loop Gain Parameters
Power on the machine and wait until the servo driver screen displays "r 0".
Press the red "SET" button; the screen will display "d01SP".
Press the blue "MODE" button; the screen will display "P00.00".
Use the arrow buttons ("◀/▲/▼") to change the parameter code to "P01.01".
Press the red "SET" button, change the parameter value 1500 to 1200, and then press the "SET" again to return to the parameter code menu. The driver will automatically save the modified parameter.
¶ Method 3. Enable Motor Adaptive Notch Filtering
If the machine exhibits the exact symptoms described above, it indicates that this specific position is a mechanical resonance point. You can automatically suppress this resonance by enabling the servo driver's adaptive notch filter function:
Check the driver parameter "P02.00" (Adaptive Notch Filter Mode Setting) and set this parameter value to "1" to turn the adaptive mode ON.
With this mode enabled, run the laser head back and forth through the resonance point 2 to 3 times. This process allows the servo motor to automatically detect the resonance frequency at that specific location and lower the gain for that frequency band, adapting the notch filter to eliminate the shaking.
Afterward, run a normal test job to see if the high-frequency vibration has disappeared and verify if the Er190 error code is resolved.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

body_text:
¶ Laser Head Jams Before Reaching Zero Point Along X-Axis - X Series
A laser head that stops before reaching the X-axis origin can interrupt processing, affect positioning accuracy, and prevent proper machine initialization. This guide explains the common causes of this issue and provides step-by-step troubleshooting instructions to restore normal X-axis movement.
¶ Problem Description
The laser head moves normally to the right along the X-axis. However, when moving to the left, the laser head stops mid-travel before reaching the zero point and cannot move any further to the left.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
A mechanical jam involving the belt, pulleys, or guide rails is blocking the path.
During reseting, the X- limit switch is triggered prematurely, causing the controller to misinterpret the position and corrupt the coordinate system.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Inspect the Motion System for Mechanical Issues
Turn OFF the machine power, then manually slide the laser head in all directions (forward, backward, left, right). Pay close attention to whether you feel a distinct resistance when moving past a specific position.
If the movement is smooth with no resistance: You can rule out a mechanical jam. Please proceed to Method 2 to check the sensor.
If you feel a noticeable jam during movement: Inspect the laser head rollers, belt teeth, and guide rails at that specific location for any trapped material debris, offcuts, or foreign objects. Remember to regularly clean and maintain these mechanical components.
¶ Method 2. Inspect the Limit Switch
¶ Step 1. Reboot or Reset the Machine
Restart the equipment or press the Reset icon on the control panel. This forces the controller to re-evaluate the zero point and coordinate positions. If this step does not restore normal operation, proceed to the next step.
¶ Step 2. Verify the Status of the Limit Switch
Attempt to move the laser head to the left again. If it still stops abruptly before reaching the origin, the X- limit switch might be triggering prematurely. Check the physical state of the limit switch at this moment to see if it has been accidentally pressed down, bent, or misaligned.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

¶ Laser Head Fails to Return to Origin After Job Completion
This guide explains how to fix situations where the laser head does not return to the origin point after a processing job is completed. If the laser head stays at the final job position or moves to the machine zero point instead of the user-defined origin, the issue is typically caused by an incorrect Return Position setting in LightBurn.
¶ Problem Description
After a processing job finishes, the laser head does not return to its origin point. Instead, it moves to the machine zero point or remains stationary at the final coordinates of the completed job.
¶ Cause
The return position setting has been modified to a different location.
¶ Solution
Open Lightburn > Machine Settings, locate the Return Position parameter, and verify that the option is correctly set to "Origin".
After making the selection, you must click "Write" to save the changes to the machine's controller.

title: Reset Failed: Laser Head Crashing Origin - X Series
excerpt: This page explains why a laser head may fail to reset properly and continuously crash into the origin position during startup. It outlines the most common causes related to switch
body_text:
¶ Reset Failed: Laser Head Constantly Crashing into the Origin - X Series
This page explains why a laser head may fail to reset properly and continuously crash into the origin position during startup. It outlines the most common causes related to switch settings and limit switch issues, along with clear, step-by-step solutions to restore normal homing behavior.
¶ Problem Description
Upon turning on the machine, the laser head fails to home correctly and continuously crashes into the origin position.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
The switch is accidentally toggled to the ON position.
The switch is physically damaged or non-functional.
The limit switch is misaligned, or the wires are incorrectly connected/loose.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Check the Rotary Axis Switch
When removing the internal packaging foam from a new machine, the rotary axis switch can sometimes be accidentally toggled. If this switch is ON, the laser head will not be able to reset normally.
Open the machine door and locate the rotary switch in the bottom right corner.
Ensure the switch is in the OFF position, then restart the machine and check if the laser head homes correctly.
¶ Method 2. Inspect the Limit Switch Status
Inspect the limit switch for any signs of physical damage, displacement or misalignment.
Open the Diagnose page on the control panel. Then press the limit switch with your finger. The corresponding button on the screen turns from green to red.
If the button remains green, the switch is faulty, please contact ONELASER After-Sales Support for a replacement part.
¶ Method 3. Check the Trigger Block on the Left Side of the Laser Head
When the laser head returns to the zero point, the trigger block on its left side is designed to trigger the X-limit switch, let the laser head stop moving. If the laser head fails to stop, inspect the trigger block to see if it has loosened or shifted out of alignment.
¶ Method 4. Verify Limit Switch Wiring
Check the connections at both the switch and the motherboard:
At the Switch: Ensure the Purple wire is correctly connected to the C port and the Yellow wire is correctly connected to the NO port.
At the Mainboard: Remove the right-side panel, locate the mainboard, and find the CN10 port. Ensure the purple and yellow wires are plugged in securely and are not loose.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Material Cannot Be Cut Through | Fix Guide - X Series
excerpt: This guide explains what to do when the material cannot be cut through during laser cutting. It outlines the most common cause—incorrect processing parameters—and provides simple s
body_text:
¶ Material Cannot Be Cut Through - X Series
This guide explains what to do when the material cannot be cut through during laser cutting. It outlines the most common cause—incorrect processing parameters—and provides simple steps to optimize speed and power for a complete and clean cut.
¶ Problem Description
During laser cutting, the material cannot be cut through
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Wrong processing parameters
If the speed is too fast and the power is too low, the cutting process will not be thorough.
Please set the correct processing parameters, you can slow down the speed and increase the power.
¶ Method 2. The minimum power setting is too low
If the areas where the laser fails to cut through consistently occur at the corners, please check your Min Power parameter. Based on the machine settings, the laser utilizes the minimum power value when navigating through corners. To cut completely through these corner areas, you must increase the Min Power value.
¶ Method 3. The reflector or focusing mirror is completely damaged
Failure to maintain the equipment on time may result in the reflector or focusing lens not being able to transmit or reflect light. Check whether the light path reflector and lens have good light transmittance.
¶ Method 4. Laser optical path deviation
The laser light path is offset, which will cause the laser to hit the inside of the laser head or the inside of the device, and the light cannot be emitted. Please use double-sided tape to stick on the three-mirror frame, and press the point shooting to check whether the light spots of the five light source points in the platform overlap.
If there is an offset, please refer to the “How to adjust the laser light path”
¶ Method 5. Incorrect focus adjustment
The bending of the material itself and the inconsistent height of the working area will cause different focal lengths at different positions in the cutting area, especially when cutting large-format patterns. Please use a strong magnet to flatten the material and use a focusing ruler to check whether the height of each area of the working platform is consistent. If it is not accurate, please use the focusing ruler to readjust the focal length.
¶ Method 6. Laser is weak or damaged
The laser life has reached its limit, resulting in a decrease in light output power
The laser life is usually between 2500–4000 hours, and the specific life depends on the actual operating conditions.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: No Response or X- Not Buffer Error After Transferring Bitmap - X Series
excerpt: This guide explains how to troubleshoot situations where a laser machine becomes unresponsive or displays an “X- Not Buffer” warning after transferring a bitmap image. It covers co
body_text:
¶ No Response or X- Not Buffer Error After Transferring Bitmap - X Series
This guide explains how to troubleshoot situations where a laser machine becomes unresponsive or displays an “X- Not Buffer” warning after transferring a bitmap image. It covers common causes such as oversized bitmap data, excessive image resolution, controller memory limitations, and incorrect LightBurn settings, along with practical solutions to restore normal processing.
¶ Problem Description
After transferring a bitmap image to the machine and pressing "Start" on the control panel, the machine does not respond, or it displays an X- Not Buffer warning.
Shrinking the physical dimensions of the bitmap inside the LightBurn canvas does not resolve the issue.
¶ Cause
¶ When the X- Not Buffer warning appears
The engraving speed set for the bitmap file is too fast for the hardware to process.
There are hidden, unused layers in the file that are accidentally still set to "Output."
The controller encountered a task-parsing logic error.
¶ When the machine does not respond at all
The bitmap's resolution is too high, exceeding the processing capability of the controller.
The controller's internal memory is nearly full, causing data corruption during file transfer.
¶ Solution
¶ Step 1. Test with a Simple Bitmap
Select a basic, low-resolution bitmap image, transfer it to the machine, and attempt to run the job.
If the simple image works perfectly, it confirms that your original file's resolution or data size is the root cause of the issue.
¶ Step 2. Reduce the Bitmap Resolution
Why shrinking the image size directly in LightBurn doesn't work？
Even though the image appears visually smaller in Lightburn, its underlying resolution and pixel density remain unchanged. Resizing it only in LightBurn means the raw data packet sent to the machine is still massive.
You must use external image editing software (such as Photoshop) to downsample the image, lower its overall resolution, and then re-import it into LightBurn.
¶ Step 3. Check the Controller's Internal Memory
A cluttered motherboard storage can bottleneck new incoming data.
Press the File button on the physical control panel. If you see a long list of previously saved files, delete some of the older projects to free up cache space, then try transferring your file again.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

body_text:
¶ OneLaser Approved Antifreeze
¶ Introduction
This page provides the official OneLaser Approved Antifreeze Guide, helping you protect your laser machine and chiller during winter or low-temperature environments. Based on our testing and research, we recommend two antifreeze solutions and outline the proper steps to prepare, mix, and circulate them safely. Following these instructions helps maintain reliable cooling performance, prevents freezing damage, and extends the lifespan of your equipment.
Based on our testing and research, we recommend adding the two antifreeze solutions recommended in this article to the chiller during winter.
¶ First-time setup: Adding coolant to the water tank (antifreeze vs. pure water)
¶ When operating environment stays above 41°F (5°C)
Recommendation: Use pure water or distilled water.
Reasoning: Within this temperature range, water provides superior thermal conductivity compared to antifreeze. Regularly replacing the water will significantly improve cooling efficiency.
¶ When operating temperature drops (entering winter)
Recommendation: As winter approaches, you can add antifreeze to the water. A 3:7 ratio is highly recommended (3 parts antifreeze to 7 parts water).
Reasoning: This specific ratio effectively prevents freezing while ensuring the system maintains sufficient cooling performance.
IMPORTANT
Before powering on the equipment, always verify that the cooling liquid level is filled up to the upper limit of the green zone on the gauge to ensure normal operation.
¶ Please read the instructions carefully and make adequate preparations before use
Turning all machine off (chiller and laser machine), drain water away from chiller and then clean the limescale.
Add the water first, then add the antifreeze liquid.
Open the chiller, let the water circulate for 5–10 minutes, then you can start work.
Note:
Antifreeze fluid can degrade over time, increasing its corrosiveness and altering its viscosity. Regular replacement is essential. We recommend changing the water every 2–3 months at room temperature. When temperatures rise above freezing, circulating cooling water can be replaced with softened water, such as distilled or purified water.
Consistency is key: Use the same antifreeze brand. While main components may be similar across brands, additive formulas can vary. Mixing different antifreeze types can lead to chemical reactions, precipitation, or bubbles.
For extended periods of non-use, drain the water from the laser tube, water chiller, and water pipes, especially for glass laser tubes. Failure to follow this procedure can result in laser tube damage, which is not covered by warranty.
¶ RV Antifreeze
This product should be used undiluted only when necessary. When freezing is not a concern, the system should be flushed and refilled with distilled water.
Link:
https://www.walmart.com/ip/Super-Tech-RV-and-Marine-Antifreeze/17179674
¶ Clariant
We recommend two models from this brand, but they need to be diluted according to the specified ratio.
¶ 1. Antifrogen N
https://www.clariant.com/en/Solutions/Products/2013/12/09/18/25/Antifrogen-N
Antifrogen® N is a liquid, tinted pale yellow, for use as a heat transfer medium in closed hot water heating systems, heat pumps and as cooling brine in industrial refrigeration equipment. Antifrogen® N is not suitable for the use in food or pharmaceutical applications. Alternatively, the use of Antifrogen® L is recommended. The product is inhibited without the use of nitrites-, amines-, borates-, silicates- and phosphates. The optimization of the corrosion inhibition system was performed without the use of CMR-substances (cancerogenic, mutagenic, reprotoxic).
¶ 2. Antifrogen L
https://www.clariant.com/en/Solutions/Products/2014/06/23/15/46/ANTIFROGEN-L
Antifrogen® L is a clear liquid, tinted blue, for use as a heat transfer medium in heat pump systems and in the food industry, e.g., in breweries, dairies, ice-cream factories, cold stores and fish processing factories. The product is inhibited without the use of nitrites-, amines-, borates-, silicates- and phosphates. The optimization of the corrosion inhibition system was performed without the use of CMR-substances (cancerogenic, mutagenic, reprotoxic).

title: Air Assist Display & PSI Adjustment Fix
excerpt: This guide explains how to troubleshoot abnormal air assist display behavior and airflow adjustment failures on ONELASER laser machines. It covers common causes such as air leaks,
body_text:
¶ Air Assist Digital Display Abnormality & Adjustment Failure - Hydra GEN2 Series
This guide explains how to troubleshoot abnormal air assist display behavior and airflow adjustment failures on ONELASER laser machines. It covers common causes such as air leaks, disconnected tubing, regulator issues, display configuration errors, and faulty electrical connections, along with step-by-step solutions to restore proper airflow control.
¶ Problem Description
1. Rotating the air assist knob clockwise or counter-clockwise results in no significant change on the digital display (fluctuations remain minimal, around ±0.1 PSI).
2. After pressing the red test button, the display remains red regardless of adjustment settings.
¶ Cause
Open Air Circuit: The external air source is off, an internal tube has detached, or there is a leak preventing pressure buildup.
Electrical Connection: Loose wiring or poor contact at the back of the digital display.
Configuration Error: Internal parameters of the digital display were accidentally modified.
Mechanical Lock: The regulator knob is in the "locked" position or the internal mechanical valve is damaged.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Inspect the External Air Source
¶ Step 1. Check the Pump/Compressor
Ensure the air pump is powered on and running.
Check the air pump specifications. If the pump is too small, the adjustment effect may not be obvious.
Check the air pump’s own pressure gauge (if it has) to ensure the output pressure is within the machine's required range.
¶ Step 2. Check External Tubing
Inspect the air tube from the air pump to the machine's Air Inlet for kinks or cuts.
Unplug and re-insert the air tube connector to ensure it is firmly seated in place.
¶ Method 2. Inspect the Internal Air Circuit
¶ Step 1. Check Tubing Inside the Machine
Open the side panel and inspect the air tubes between the back of the digital display, the solenoid valve, and the regulator valve. Check specifically for tubes that may have slipped off due to long-term vibration or airflow blockages caused by an excessively small bending radius.
¶ Step 2. Check the Solenoid Valve Outlet
Disconnect the air tube at the solenoid valve outlet and feel if there is a strong airflow being ejected. If not, the solenoid valve is damaged or not receiving a trigger signal.
¶ Step 3. Check the Regulator Valve Outlet
With the air source connected, turn the adjustment knob. Disconnect the air tube leading from the regulator valve to the cutting head and test whether the airflow intensity changes as the knob is turned. If the airflow remains constant or there is no air output, the pressure regulator valve is internally damaged.
¶ Method 3. Check the Digital Display
¶ Step 1. Check the Digital Display Settings (Factory Standard)
Note: If you need to change options or values in the settings during this process, you must first set 1-P and 2-P in Step ② to 0.
① Long-press the SET key to enter the settings menu. Click the SET key to switch between setting items, and use the Up/Down keys next to it to change options/values. Verify the settings match the table below:
Setting Item
Option / Value
Explanation
ot1 / ot2
EASY
Two output modes: Easy Mode
noC
1o2o
Output state: 1 and 2 are both Normally Open
SPD
100
Output response time: 100ms

r-on
Output color: Red when outputting
Unt
PSI
Pressure unit: Pounds per square inch
② Click the SET key again and set the values for 1-P and 2-P to 0.3. This value determines at what pressure the display changes color, typically used to indicate if the airflow meets working requirements.
¶ Step 2. Check the Mechanical Status of Buttons and Knobs
If you find the display lights up even without pressing the red button, please troubleshoot according to this FAQ: Test button always on, unable to adjust airflow
The adjustment knobs on the Hydra Gen2 usually feature a "pull up to unlock, press down to lock" design. If you cannot rotate it, try gently pulling the knob upward. If it is stuck, you can use a tool to help pull it up, after which it should return to normal operation.
¶ Step 3. Check the Wiring at the Back
Inspect the plug or wiring terminals behind the digital display. Gently tug the cables to confirm the terminal screws are tightened. If the wiring has poor contact, the digital display may show jumping values or a black screen due to unstable voltage.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Touchscreen Alarm Guide for X Series - XRF/ XT
excerpt: This document provides an overview of common alarm messages that may appear on the One Laser touchscreen interface. These alerts are designed to protect the machine, ensure operati
body_text:
¶ Touchscreen Alarm Guide for X Series - XRF/ XT
This document provides an overview of common alarm messages that may appear on the One Laser touchscreen interface. These alerts are designed to protect the machine, ensure operational stability, and assist users in identifying potential risks during laser processing. Because the device firmware is continually updated, users may occasionally encounter pop-up messages not yet included in this guide.
¶ 1. X- or Y-Axis Boundary Exceeded
¶ Overview
The machine will issue an “out-of-bounds” alarm when the design file extends beyond the physical working limits of the device. For example, the X Series model provides a processing area of 600 × 300 mm. When either axis exceeds this range, the system interrupts job execution to prevent mechanical collision or excessive travel.
¶ Why This Happens
This alert commonly arises from:
A design file larger than the available workspace
Hidden graphics in the design are set to "Output"
Incorrect origin selection that shifts the design outside the valid working area
Misalignment caused by offsetting the starting point too close to an edge
In the reference diagram provided with the machine, the yellow region represents the machine’s working boundary, the green square indicates the user-defined origin, and the blue/gray areas denote the file’s placement.
If the origin is selected incorrectly—such as the example where it is set near the edge—the file may partially fall outside the allowable range, triggering the alarm.
¶ Recommended Actions
Verify that the design dimensions fall within the permitted workspace.
Check for hidden layers or graphics and toggle the "Output" setting to OFF
Reset the origin and ensure that the entire file lies safely within the machine’s processing area.
¶ 2. Insufficient Buffer Distance
¶ Overview
During engraving, the laser head requires a certain amount of buffer space to accelerate, decelerate, and execute rapid directional changes. If the file is positioned too close to the boundary of the working area, the machine may detect insufficient buffer distance and trigger a warning.
¶ Why This Happens
This alert is typically caused by:
A file placed extremely close to the workspace edges
An origin location that does not leave the head enough space for motion planning
The bitmap resolution is too high, causing data errors during file transfer to the device. (The transfer may appear successful, but this alarm will trigger once processing begins)
¶ Recommended Actions
Adjust the origin to give the design additional margin from the machine’s physical limits.
Re-run the job once sufficient buffer distance has been ensured.
Use professional software (such as Photoshop) to reduce the resolution of the bitmap.
¶ 3. Water Protection Trigger (XT Series)
¶ Overview
The XT Series utilizes a glass CO₂ laser tube paired with a water-cooling system. To protect the tube from overheating, the machine incorporates a water-flow sensor. When this sensor fails to detect water movement at the beginning of a job, the system displays a water-protection alarm. This prevents tube damage and ensures long-term operational safety.
¶ Inspection Point
To access the water-cooling components, open the rear housing using an M2 screwdriver.
¶ Recommended Actions
Confirm that the water pump’s signal cable is properly connected.
Check whether the water pump is operating normally and providing consistent flow.
¶ 4. Combined Alarm Window
(Door Cover Protection / Flame Alarm / Water Temperature Alarm)
Several safety-related alerts share a common pop-up interface. When this window appears, users should assess the possible causes one by one.
¶ 4.1 Door Cover Protection
¶ Overview
For safety reasons, the device requires all doors and covers to remain fully closed during operation. If any cover is open or not securely latched, the system issues a door-protection alarm and stops the job.
¶ Recommended Action:
Ensure that all covers and access panels are completely closed before restarting the process.
Disable "Enable door open protect" in LightBurn > Machine Settings
If the alarm stops, it confirms the issue lies with the Door Cover Sensor.
If the alarm persists, continue troubleshooting with the steps below.
¶ 4.2 Water Temperature Alarm
¶ Overview
When the water temperature inside the cooling tank exceeds 45 °C, the machine automatically halts operation and emits a beeping sound. This prevents thermal damage to the laser tube, which is sensitive to elevated temperatures.
¶ Recommended Action:
Wait until the water temperature falls back to a safe range before resuming work.
Check for loose wiring connections on the motherboard.
¶ 4.3 Flame Alarm
¶ Overview
The system includes a flame-detection sensor that monitors for abnormal combustion events within the workspace. If the sensor detects a flame or receives an irregular signal, the machine will stop immediately for safety.
¶ Diagnostic Steps
Inspect the flame-detection probe to ensure it is not bent or obstructed, and verify that all wiring is intact.
Open the right-side panel (remove the cover with a screwdriver).
Locate the intelligent control board and disconnect the IN6 interface.
Restart the machine:
If the beeping alarm persists even after IN6 is disconnected, the control board may have malfunctioned and should be evaluated by technical support.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: LightBurn Camera Not Detected Fix - X Series
excerpt: This guide explains how to troubleshoot situations where the XRF camera does not appear or cannot be used inside LightBurn. Camera detection issues are commonly caused by USB conne
body_text:
¶ Camera Not Available in LightBurn - X Series
This guide explains how to troubleshoot situations where the XRF camera does not appear or cannot be used inside LightBurn. Camera detection issues are commonly caused by USB connection problems, unstable hardware connections, software recognition failures, or camera module defects. Follow the steps below to identify and resolve the issue.
¶ Problem Description
The XRF camera cannot be used, and the camera device does not appear inside LightBurn.
¶ Cause
Damaged USB connection cable
Faulty USB hub or docking station (If you use it)
Loose camera-side cable connection
Insufficient solder on the camera board solder joints
The computer cannot properly recognize the camera device
Using the macOS version of LightBurn, where camera connections may occasionally be unstable
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Hardware Inspection
¶ Step 1. Replace the Original USB Cable
Try replacing the current USB cable with another known-good USB data cable. If the camera appears after replacing the cable, the original cable may be damaged internally.
¶ Step 2. Test the Original Cable with Another Device
Use the original USB cable with another USB device. If the second device also cannot be recognized, the USB cable is likely defective.
¶ Step 3. Change the Computer USB Port
If you are using a USB hub or a docking station, connect the XRF camera directly to the computer instead. Some USB hubs or docking stations may provide unstable power or insufficient data bandwidth for the camera.
You can slso try different USB ports on the computer, or USB 2.0 and USB 3.0 ports separately.
¶ Method 2. Camera Module Inspection
¶ Step 1. Check the Camera Connector and Wiring
Inspect the camera-side connector carefully. Please check for: Loose connectors, partially inserted cables and damaged wires. Then reconnect the cable firmly and test again.

title: Fix Charring at Corners & Start Points - Hydra Series
excerpt: This guide explains how to eliminate burn marks and charred spots that appear at corners and starting points during laser cutting. These defects are typically caused by heat buildu
body_text:
¶ Excessive Charring at Corners and Start Points - Hydra Series
This guide explains how to eliminate burn marks and charred spots that appear at corners and starting points during laser cutting. These defects are typically caused by heat buildup due to speed and power mismatches. By optimizing cutting parameters and airflow, you can achieve cleaner edges and more consistent results.
¶ Problem Description
During cutting, prominent burn marks or charred spots appear specifically at the starting point and the corners of the graphic.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
If the laser maintains high power while moving slowly or dwelling in one spot, it causes localized heat accumulation and over-burning.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Add Lead-in and Lead-out Lines
When the laser first fires, there is an instantaneous power surge before the laser head reaches its programmed speed. This "low speed + high power" combination causes over-burning.
Please enable Lead-in and Lead-out in your layer settings. This allows the laser to start firing on a small sacrificial path outside your actual design, ensuring the head is at the correct speed by the time it reaches your cut line.
¶ Method 2. Reduce the Min Power Value
At sharp corners, the controller slows down the laser head. The Min Power setting determines the output during these slower moments.
Please lower the Min Power (%) value in your Cut Settings Layers. By reducing power as the machine slows down for a turn, you can achieve a much more uniform edge and prevent corner melting or charring.
¶ Method 3. Optimize Air Assist
Charring is often caused by the combustion of material vapors. If you have an Air Assist Kit installed, increase the airflow setting. Stronger airflow blows away smoke and rapidly cools the cutting area, significantly reducing burnt edges.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: X-axis or Y-axis Cannot Move - X Series
excerpt: The laser head suddenly stops moving along the X-axis or Y-axis during a job.
body_text:
¶ X-axis or Y-axis Cannot Move - X Series
¶ Problem Description
The laser head suddenly stops moving along the X-axis or Y-axis during a job.
When the machine is powered on, tapping the movement buttons on the control panel does not cause the laser head to move along the X-axis or Y-axis.
The laser head is unable to move along the Y-axis after switching from the rotary axis back to normal flatbed processing.
The machine has just arrived, and upon powering it on for the first time, the laser head is unable to move along the X-axis or Y-axis.
¶ Cause
The plug for the X-axis or Y-axis driver is loose or burned out.
The wire connected to the X-axis or Y-axis driver is loose or the wire is broken internally.
The wire plugs on both sides of the X-axis or Y-axis motor are loose.
The X-axis or Y-axis motor is broken.
The rotary axis switch was not turned OFF after using the rotary axis.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Inspect the X-Axis or Y-Axis Driver
Disconnect the power. Unscrew the screws on the right side of the XRF and remove the right side cover.
Locate the X-axis/Y-axis driver (near the back end of the machine).
Step 1. Check if the signal cables are plugged into the correct ports
Check whether the signal cables on the X, Y, and Z axis drivers are correctly plugged into the ports (as shown in the image).
Step 2. Check for any loose or burned connections at the driver plug
If the plug is loose: Push the plug in tightly, ensuring a secure connection. Then, try moving the X-axis or Y-axis.
If the plug is burned: Take photos and contact customer service via ZOHO to request a replacement for the damaged driver plug (if the machine is still under warranty).
¶ Method 2. Check the Wiring on the Driver
Prepare a multimeter and set it to continuity mode. Turn the machine OFF and unplug the wires from the driver.
Use the multimeter probes to check continuity on:
① Black and Yellow & Green wires
② Brown and Blue wires
The multimeter should beep or display "0L" to confirm continuity.
The diagram below illustrates checking the Y-axis driver as an example.
¶ Method 3. Inspect the X-Axis or Y-Axis Motor
Locate the X-axis motor and verify the wire plug is securely connected.
Open the cover at the back of the honeycomb board to locate the Y-axis motor. Check if the wire plug is connected and if the motor is functioning.
¶ Method 4. Check the Power Status
With the machine ON, gently slide the gantry. If it moves freely with no resistance, the motors may not be receiving power.
¶ Method 5. Check the Rotary Axis Toggle Switch (Specific to Y-Axis Issues)
Locate the rotary axis toggle switch inside the machine. If it is in the ON position, the Y-axis motor will not receive power.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Fix Smoke Leakage & Exhaust Issues
excerpt: This guide explains how to resolve smoke leakage issues during laser processing by optimizing your machine’s exhaust and airflow system. If smoke is escaping from the enclosure ins
body_text:
¶ Smoke Escaping During Processing: Exhaust Optimization - X Series
This guide explains how to resolve smoke leakage issues during laser processing by optimizing your machine’s exhaust and airflow system. If smoke is escaping from the enclosure instead of being properly vented, it indicates an imbalance in airflow. The following methods will help you achieve efficient smoke extraction and maintain a cleaner working environment.
¶ Problem Description
Smoke and dust are leaking out of the machine during operation instead of being vented properly. This results in poor air quality and high readings on the PM2.5 Detector.
¶ Cause
The core issue is an imbalance in air pressure between the inside and outside of the machine:
Insufficient Air Assist: The air pump provides inadequate intake pressure to push smoke toward the exhaust.
Inadequate Extraction: The exhaust fan is underpowered or installed in an inefficient position.
¶ Solution
¶ Principle
Efficient venting requires a balance of airflow.
Positive Pressure: If the internal pressure is higher than the external environment but the exhaust fan is weak, smoke will be forced out of every gap and seal in the chassis.
Negative Pressure: If the exhaust fan is strong but there is no fresh air intake (Air Assist), the vacuum effect will actually reduce the overall displacement efficiency, causing smoke to swirl and eventually leak.
¶ Method 1. Upgrade or Inspect the Air Pump
For consistent, high-volume production, the standard small air pump may not be sufficient.
We suggest using a high-power Air Compressor to maintain stable intake pressure. This helps "push" the smoke toward the back of the machine where the exhaust intake is located.
¶ Method 2. Optimize the Exhaust Fan
Based on our lab standards, we recommend that your exhaust fan meets the following these specifications:
(Note: Hydra Series machines require even higher specs)
Airflow:
366m3/h
Static Pressure:
578Pa
Speed:
3800RPM
Installation Position Matters:
Flexible Hoses: If using flexible ducting, install the fan closest to the machine. This creates immediate suction at the source to pull smoke out before it can dissipate.
Rigid Piping: If using hard/rigid pipes, you can install the fan at the end of the duct (farthest from the machine) to pull the smoke through the system more effectively.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
