¶ Touchscreen Function Introduction
This guide provides a complete overview of the touchscreen control panel and the function of each button. It helps users understand the interface, navigate different pages, and operate the machine efficiently during setup, manual control, and job processing.
¶ Introduction
This document offers a comprehensive guide to the functions of each button on the control panel, ensuring a thorough understanding of their operations.

Z axis button: Control the table to move in Z axis
Direction button: Control the laser head to move in X and Y axis

Esc button: Exit the current state

Preview image: Preview effect of the current file
Name: The name of the file
Power setting: Max power and min power
Working time: The running time of this job
Speed setting: Running speed of your job

Processing progress: Check the processing status of the job

Air assist: It will be displayed when the machine is in standard mode. Intelligent mode as default settings
Exhaust: It will be displayed when the machine is in standard mode

body_text:
¶ Laser Maintenance Guide & Checklist
This Laser Maintenance Guide provides a complete checklist for cleaning and servicing your laser machine. It covers optical maintenance, hardware care, external device maintenance, and a recommended maintenance plan to ensure stable performance, longer component lifespan, and consistent engraving and cutting quality.
¶ Optical Maintenance
¶ Tools Required
Lens cleaner, Cotton swabs (Q-tip), Hex key
If the provided cleaning solution runs out, use absolute ethanol to clean the lens. Do not use isopropyl alcohol, as it may damage the lens coating.
If cotton swabs are unavailable, use a soft, lint-free cloth or high-quality cotton swabs.
¶ Mirror 1 Cleaning
Step 1: Power off the machine.
Step 2: Unscrew the rear cover screws and remove the rear case cover.
Step 3: Loosen the screws securing the reflector and remove Mirror 1.
Step 4: Use a cotton swab soaked with optics cleaning fluid to clean the surface.
Step 5: Use a clean, dry cotton swab to remove any remaining moisture or residue.
¶ Beam Combiner Cleaning
Step 1: Use a cotton swab soaked with optics cleaning fluid.
Step 2: Wipe gently and finish with a clean, dry swab to remove water spots.
¶ Mirror 2 Cleaning
Step 1: Loosen the screws securing the reflector and remove Mirror 2.
Step 2: Clean with a cotton swab soaked in optics cleaning fluid.
Step 3: Wipe dry with a clean cotton swab.
¶ Mirror 3 Cleaning
Step 1: Remove the front cover of the laser head.
Step 2: Clean the mirror with a cotton swab soaked in optics cleaning fluid.
Step 3: Use a dry swab to remove any remaining moisture.
¶ Focusing Lens Cleaning
Step 1: Remove the focusing lens mount.
Step 2: Clean the lens with a cotton swab soaked in optics cleaning fluid.
Step 3: Dry gently with a clean cotton swab.
¶ Hardware Maintenance
¶ Tools Required
Lubricating oil
Air blow gun (self-provided)
Soft brushes (self-provided)
Rags (self-provided)
¶ Auto Sensor
Step 1: Blow away large dust particles using an air blow gun.
Step 2: Use a dry cloth to remove remaining dirt from the sensor.
¶ Rails, Belts, Gears, Rollers
Step 1: Blow away large dust particles with an air blow gun.
Step 2: Wipe rails and belts with a dry cloth.
Step 3: Use an alcohol-dampened cloth to finish cleaning.
Step 4: Clean gears and rollers with a dry cloth, then wipe with an alcohol-dampened cloth.
¶ Screw Rods
Step 1: Wipe the screw rod with a dry cloth to remove dirt.
Step 2: Apply a small amount of lubricant to the top of the screw rod.
Raise and lower the laser head to distribute lubricant evenly.
Do not use excessive lubricant, as this can attract dust and dirt.
¶ Scrap Drawer
Remove the waste drawer and empty its contents regularly to prevent debris buildup.
¶ Cooling Fan
Step 1: Blow away large dust particles from the fan using an air blow gun.
Step 2: Use a dry cloth to clean dust residue from the fan blades.
¶ Laser Head Blow-Off Nozzle
Step 1: Turn the blow-off nozzle counterclockwise to remove it.
Step 2: Clean with a cloth soaked in cleaning solution.
¶ External Device Maintenance
¶ Tools Required
Air blow gun, Water pump
¶ Exhaust Fan
Step 1: Remove the screws securing the exhaust fan.
Disconnect the power supply to the fan.
Step 2: Use an air gun to blow dust off the fan blades.
¶ Chiller (XT Model)
Step 1: Turn the water tank cap counterclockwise to open it.
Step 2: Use a water pump to drain the water.
Step 3: Refill with distilled water.
If the room temperature is too low, add approved antifreeze.
The chiller must be filled with distilled water or pure water only.
¶ Dust Filter Cotton
Use an air gun to clean the dust filter cotton located on the rear cover.

title: How to Use the Laser Camera in LightBurn
excerpt: How to Use the Camera is a complete operation guide designed to help you connect, configure, and use your laser camera with LightBurn software. This guide walks you through USB com
body_text:
¶ How to Use the Camera
How to Use the Camera is a complete operation guide designed to help you connect, configure, and use your laser camera with LightBurn software. This guide walks you through USB communication, calibration import, overlay alignment, and trace extraction to ensure accurate pattern positioning and processing.
¶ Attention
The camera can only communicate via USB cable.
¶ Operation Guide
Step 1: After switching on the machine, connect your computer to the machine using the USB cable and the camera cable.
Step 2: Start the LightBurn software and confirm that the machine is communicating successfully with the software. If the “Ready” sign is displayed, communication has been successful.
Absolute coordinates are recommended to ensure more accurate processing.
Step 3: Remove the cover from the camera.
Step 4: Place the paper from which the pattern is to be extracted on the honeycomb bed and close the top cover of the machine after completing autofocus.
Note: It is recommended to place the paper on a hard board to prevent it from being pressed into the honeycomb holes due to its thinness while the laser head is completing autofocus, which could cause distortion.
Step 5: Click on “Camera Control” to open the camera function.
Step 6: In camera selection, select the camera with the name corresponding to the LightBurn camera.
Step 7: Right-click and select “Import Camera Settings” to import the camera calibration file from the U disk.
Step 8: Click “Update Overlay” to update the pattern on the canvas.
Step 9: Click “Trace” to select the range of the pattern to be extracted by adjusting the threshold. After adjustment, click “OK” to capture the pattern.
Step 10: After selecting the extracted pattern, set the processing parameters and click “Frame,” then start processing.

Make sure the machine sits evenly on the base without tilting.

If you plan to use the pass-through door feature:

Ensure the structural setup is complete before operation

Double-check that all mounting points are secure

body_text:
¶ How to Switch between Different Focusing Mirrors
The Hydra series of lasers come standard with a 2.5-inch focusing lens, with optional lenses available in 1.5-inch, 2.0-inch, and 4.0-inch sizes. This document will guide you on how to replace the different sizes of focusing lenses.
¶ Preparation
OneLaser Hydra Series device*1
Focusing lens and focusing lens barrel to be switched
¶ Distinguishing between different focusing cartridges
Different focusing lenses fit different focusing cartridges, and the cartridges are labeled with the corresponding lens type.
If you need to replace the focusing lens, please make sure you have purchased the appropriate focusing lens and matching focusing lens barrel.
¶ Instructions for switching the focusing lens
¶ Remove the focusing lens barrel
Hold down the air tube connector while pulling the air tube upward. As shown in the figure.
Loosen the gold-colored nut holding the lens barrel counterclockwise. Make sure to hold the laser head with your hand during this process to prevent it from falling.
Continue to rotate the mirror barrel counterclockwise until the barrel separates from the laser cone head.
¶ Assemble the new focusing lens barrel
The focusing mirror needs to be installed in the barrel.
Note: Focusing lens is mounted with the convex side up.
Remove the locating rubber ring from the removed barrel and install it on the barrel to be replaced.
Install the focusing lens barrel to be replaced by tightening it clockwise on the laser cone head.
Connect the air hose and reinstall the laser head.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis.

body_text:
¶ Calibrate the Optical Path of the Red Indicator Light - Hydra Series
This guide explains how to calibrate the red indicator light so it aligns precisely with the actual laser beam. Proper alignment ensures accurate positioning, improves engraving precision, and reduces setup errors during operation.
¶ Tools you need to prepare
M2.5 hexagon socket screwdriver ×1
Double-sided tape ×1
Machine door cover key ×1
¶ Preparations before calibration
Turn on the machine and move the laser head to the center position of the platform.
Click Menu → Alignment → Uncheck Pulse time → Set Power to 20%.
Take a piece of double-sided tape and stick it on the left side of the laser head, then press and hold the “Pulse” button (for about 0.5 seconds) to make a spot on the double-sided tape.
¶ Calibrate the red light path
The red light indicator is located at the upper left corner of the platform. You need to use the door cover key to open the upper left door cover of the machine.
Use a hex screwdriver to rotate the adjustment screw shown in the figure to correct the red light path.
When the red light and the light spot are completely aligned, the calibration process is complete.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

USB cable ×1

2. Connect the Hydra with lightburn, for the connection steps, please click on the link below to watch the tutorial Getting Started With LightBurn: Getting Started With LightBurn: Set up & First Project

Note: Remove the cover of the camera before use.

¶ The Machine Emits Abnormal Light - Hydra Series
This page explains why the laser may fire abnormally when the machine is powered on. It outlines common causes related to incorrect controller wiring or software configuration and provides step-by-step instructions to correct signal connections and factory settings.
¶ Problem Description
The laser fires abnormally when the machine is powered on.
¶ Cause
Incorrect Controller Ports: The laser signal cables are plugged into the wrong ports on the motherboard.
Incorrect Software Configuration: The laser signal parameters in the factory settings are misconfigured.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Verify Laser Signal Output Connections
Open the bottom door panel on the right side of the machine to access the controller. Check if the terminals are connected correctly according to the wiring diagram.
¶ For machines with old firmware:
When using a dual light source system, the Glass tube and the RF tube must share Port ②.
When switching between light sources, you must manually unplug the existing signal terminal from Port ② and then connect the signal terminal for the other light source.
Installation Tip: Ensure the terminals are seated correctly by plugging them as far to the right of the port as possible.
¶ For machines with the latest software/firmware updates:
Please identify and connect the terminals according to the updated configuration below:
¶ Method 2. Verify Software Laser Signal Settings
Connect the machine to your computer and open RDWorks. Navigate to File > Factory Settings (Password may be required; usually RD8888).
Setup laser config:
For Laser config, select Multi tube,
Select Laser 1 type to Glass tube
Select Laser 2 type to RF Laser (preginition)
Make sure other config is same to screenshot below (mark as step 4)
Click Write and wait until progress complete (mark as step 5)
Critical Check:
Verify that Laser Type 1 is Glass Tube and Laser Type 2 is RF Tube CO2 (Pre-combustion). The switch signal level must be set to High.

excerpt: This page explains how to properly adjust the X-axis of your laser machine. It covers belt tension balancing and axis alignment to correct skewing, uneven movement, or positioning
body_text:
¶ Adjustment of the X-axis - Hydra Series
This page explains how to properly adjust the X-axis of your laser machine. It covers belt tension balancing and axis alignment to correct skewing, uneven movement, or positioning errors. Follow the steps carefully to ensure smooth motion and accurate cutting or engraving results.
¶ Tools required
M2,3,4 hexagonal wrench ×1
5.5mm open-end wrench ×1
Note: Please complete the following operations under power-off condition and keep the removed screws properly to avoid loss.
¶ Procedure
¶ Step 1. Adjust the belt (if the belt elasticity is the same on both sides there is no need to operate)
Set the tension of the belts on both sides to the same level
Unlock the nut first with a 5.5mm open end wrench.
Adjust the internal screws with M2 hexagonal wrench, tighten the belt by turning inward, loosen the belt by turning outward.
Adjusted to check whether the two sides of the belt elasticity is consistent, you can press the belt by hand, and at the same time check whether the gap between the two sides of the screws is consistent.
Tighten the nut after adjustment.
¶ Step 2. Adjustment of X-axis
If the x-axis is skewed on this side, you need to adjust the parts on this side, and similarly if it is on the other side, adjust the other side.
Unlock this side of the coupling first.
Loosen the screws on the bottom of the y-axis slider (there are 4 of them).
Pull the entire X-axis to the bottom, with the bottom aligned with the tensioning seat.
Hold the X-axis by hand and lock the coupling.
Lock the screws on the bottom of the y-axis slider.
Finally, push the x-axis to move and check for anomalies.
Important Reminder:

title: Laser Stops During Processing - X Series
excerpt: This page explains why a laser machine may suddenly stop before a job is complete. It covers the most common causes, including safety triggers, incorrect layer settings, limit swit
body_text:
¶ Laser Head Stops Moving - X Series
This page explains why a laser machine may suddenly stop before a job is complete. It covers the most common causes, including safety triggers, incorrect layer settings, limit switch activation, and memory limitations, along with step-by-step solutions to restore normal operation.
¶ Problem Description
The machine suddenly stops during processing, and the laser head ceases all movement before the job is complete.
¶ Cause
Door Protection Triggered: The system detects that a cover or door has been opened, triggering safety mode.
Layer Parameter Error: Speed settings for one or more layers are set too low (near zero).
Limit Switch Triggered: The laser head has hit a physical limit during the movement path.
Insufficient Memory: Too many files stored on the device have exhausted the available memory.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Verify All Covers are Closed
Click OK on the control panel to exit the system protection state. Ensure all doors and covers are securely closed before starting or restarting a job to maintain a safe working environment.
¶ Method 2. Check Layer Parameters
Check if any layer has an extremely low speed setting. If the speed is too low, the laser head may move so slowly that it appears to have stopped.
¶ Method 3. Perform a System Reset
This is usually caused by a coordinate system mismatch, where the controller's internal position (A, B) does not match the physical position (C, D), causing it to hit a limit switch.
Press the Reset button on the physical control panel to re-home the machine. After resetting, verify that the origin and coordinate system have returned to normal.
¶ Method 4. Check Max Travel Values
Please verify that the Max Travel values for the X and Y axes in Machine Settings match your machine's actual work area dimensions. If you are unsure of the correct dimensions, please contact ONELASER After-Sales Support to confirm the factory specifications.
¶ Method 5. Manage Device Memory
Memory status cannot be checked directly on the control panel. Please connect the machine to LightBurn. Open the File List via the software and delete old or unnecessary files to free up storage space.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Laser Head No Red Dot Indicator - Hydra Series
excerpt: This page explains why the red dot indicator may not appear when the machine is powered on or during operation. It covers the most common causes, including indicator failure, loose
body_text:
¶ Laser Head Without Red Dot Indication - Hydra Series
This page explains why the red dot indicator may not appear when the machine is powered on or during operation. It covers the most common causes, including indicator failure, loose connections, or power supply issues, and provides step-by-step troubleshooting to restore the red dot function.
¶ Problem Description
The red light indicator is not visible while the machine is powered on or during normal operation. The laser may still function, but the absence of the red dot makes positioning and alignment difficult.
¶ Cause
The red light indicator itself has failed.
The connector for the indicator is loose or poorly seated.
The TL-Timer board is not providing the necessary voltage.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Check the Red Dot Indicator
Open the top door on the left side of the machine. Locate the red light mounting bracket (near the beam combiner) and check if the red light is emitting light from the source.
If the Light is ON: If you see light at the source but not on the workbed, the reflective mirrors may be dirty or oxidized after prolonged use, failing to reflect the red light. Clean and maintain your mirrors.
If the Light is OFF: If no light is emitted at the source, proceed with the following electrical troubleshooting:
¶ Method 2. Inspect the Indicator Connector
Locate the red light indicator adapter interface (as shown in the diagram) and check for a loose or poor connection.
Note: The adapter interface is located on the left side of the machine, near the beam combiner.
If the connections are secure but the light remains off, test the power supply:
Open the bottom door panel on the right side of the machine. Locate the TL-Timer board and unplug the wires indicated in the wiring diagram.
Set your multimeter to the 5V DC range and measure the output voltage at those pins.
If the voltage is 5V: The TL-Timer board is working correctly, but the red light indicator component is faulty and needs to be replaced.
If the voltage is NOT 5V: The TL-Timer board is faulty and needs to be replaced.
Support: Please contact the ONELASER After-Sales Team to request the necessary replacement parts based on your test results.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

body_text:
¶ Broken or Intermittent Lines During Cutting or Scanning - X Series
¶ Problem Description
During cutting or scanning, the line becomes broken or incomplete, and the laser head fires intermittently. A clicking sound from the machine can often be heard as it attempts to fire. The processing speed and power parameters are set normally.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
Computer Memory: Insufficient system memory or high memory usage causing data packet loss.
USB Stability: Unstable USB connection due to electromagnetic interference.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Switch Connection Method
Restart your computer to free up system memory.
Connect the machine via Ethernet or Wi-Fi instead of USB.
Click the links below to view the connection tutorials:
Connect XT & XRF to LightBurn via Ethernet
Connect XT & XRF to LightBurn via Wi-Fi
¶ Method 2. XT Model: Low Water Level or Damaged Water Sensor
Low Water Level：
Open the back panel of the machine to locate the cooling system. Look at the water level sensor. If the water is low, you will likely notice that the red light on the sensor is off. Add the water until the level reaches the bottom of the neck line. Once the water is at the correct level, check the sensor again to see if the red light has turned back on.
Damaged Water Sensor：
Turn off the machine and locate the TL-Timing board.
Unplug the yellow-green wire indicated by the red arrow in the image. Then use a conductive material to short-circuit IN11 and GND on the board.
After shorting, check whether the laser fault (no beam output) still occurs when running a job.
While the machine is running, check the water sensor status. If the status is unclear, record a video and contact the OneLaser customer service team for further assistance.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

excerpt: Laser Replacement is a complete maintenance guide covering both glass tube replacement (XT models) and RF tube replacement (XRF models). This page walks you through safe disassembl
body_text:
¶ Laser Replacement
Laser Replacement is a complete maintenance guide covering both glass tube replacement (XT models) and RF tube replacement (XRF models). This page walks you through safe disassembly, proper installation, and optical path alignment to ensure stable laser performance and long machine lifespan.
¶ Safety Notes
The following operations must be performed after power is disconnected.
Please store removed screws properly to avoid loss.
¶ Disassembly of the Enclosure
Both XT and XRF models require disassembly of the enclosure.
Use an M2 hex wrench to remove the screws on the rear cover, then remove the rear cover.
¶ Glass Tube Replacement (XT)
¶ 1. Tools Required
Hex wrench
Steel ruler
Water pump
Utility knife
¶ 2. Drain the Water Tank
Step 1: Unscrew the water tank cap counterclockwise.
Step 2: Use a water pump to drain all water from the tank.
¶ 3. Disassembly of the Glass Tube
Step 1: Measure the distance from the glass tube to Mirror 1 using a steel ruler and record it.
Step 2: Unscrew the positive and negative electrode wires counterclockwise.
Step 3: Use a utility knife to cut the zip ties at the water inlet and outlet, then remove the water pipes.
Step 4: Remove the two screws securing the laser tube and carefully take out the glass tube.
¶ 4. Install the Glass Tube
Step 1: Place the new glass tube onto the laser holder and adjust the distance to Mirror 1 using the previously recorded measurement.
Step 2: Secure the laser tube with screws and tighten the fixing tape.
Step 3: Reconnect the inlet and outlet water pipes and secure them with zip ties.
Step 4: Reconnect the positive and negative electrode wires.
Step 5: Adjust the optical path (refer to the Optical Path Adjustment Tutorial).
¶ RF Tube Replacement (XRF)
¶ 1. Tools Required
Hex wrench
Phillips screwdriver
¶ 2. Disassembly of the RF Tube
Step 1: Unplug the power cable, fan power cable, and signal cable.
Step 2: Rotate counterclockwise to remove the beam expander.
Step 3: Remove the screws securing the RF tube and take out the RF tube.
Step 4: Use a hex wrench to remove the beam expander mirror holder.
¶ 3. Installation of the RF Tube
Step 1: Install the beam expander mirror holder onto the new RF tube.
Step 2: Secure the RF tube to the mounting bracket.
Step 3: Reconnect the power cable, fan power cable, and signal cable.
Step 4: Install the beam expander.
Step 5: Adjust the optical path (refer to the Optical Path Adjustment Tutorial).

¶ How to Focus a Laser Machine
The automatic focusing method uses contact-based focusing. Soft materials may affect the focusing accuracy (e.g., sponge, leather). For soft materials, please use manual focusing.
You can use 6 mm acrylic to make a focusing ruler.
File: 6mm focusing ruler.dxf (104.6KB)
¶ Manual Focus
Place the material on the honeycomb panel and fix it, then move the laser head above the material.
Use a focusing ruler to focus. The focus distance is 6 mm.
¶ Auto Focus
1. Place the material on the honeycomb panel and fix it, then move the laser head above the material.
2. Press the autofocus button on the screen and wait for the focus to complete.
¶ Note
Please ensure you only press the autofocus button once for each autofocus operation.
Since there is no lower limit on the Z-axis of the machine, if the honeycomb table is removed, you must place material underneath when using autofocus or pressing down to focus.
Otherwise, this may cause machine and laser head collisions.

title: Engraved Text with Hollow Centers or Broken Lines
excerpt: This page explains why engraved text may appear hollow, incomplete, or disconnected during laser processing. It focuses on common LightBurn text and font vector issues and provides
body_text:
¶ Engraved Text with Hollow Centers or Broken Lines
This page explains why engraved text may appear hollow, incomplete, or disconnected during laser processing. It focuses on common LightBurn text and font vector issues and provides clear, step-by-step solutions to ensure engraved text is solid, continuous, and production-ready.
¶ Problem Description
Engraved text samples contain hollow centers (missing fill) or disconnected segments where the lines should be continuous.
¶ Cause
The text pattern settings in LightBurn are incorrectly configured or the font vectors are overlapping.
¶ Solution
¶ Convert Text to Path
Method 1：Select your text, then go to the top menu and click Edit → Convert to Path.
Method 2：Select the text, right-click, and choose Convert to Path from the pop-up menu.
Why should you convert Font to Path?
If you open the file on a different computer or a different software version that lacks the original font, the system might automatically substitute it, causing deformation or layout errors. Converting to a Path locks the shape permanently.
A Path represents the actual physical movement trajectory, whereas a Font is a software calculation. Converting to a Path reduces redundant paths and unexpected jumps, which is critical for fine detail.
For mass production, Path data is more stable and ensures consistent results across multiple jobs.
⚠️Important Note:
Once converted to a Path, the text content can no longer be edited as text (you cannot change the spelling or font). It is highly recommended to keep a Original Text Version backup file before converting.
¶ Weld Shapes
If your text appears hollow because the characters overlap, you need to merge the overlapping vectors.
Method 1：Select the converted path, then go to the top menu and click Tools → Weld Shapes.
Method 2：Select the path and find the Weld Shapes icon in the left-hand toolbar.
¶ Test Result Comparison

title: How to Adjust Backlash Parameters in LightBurn
excerpt: Backlash and scan offset issues can cause misaligned lines, blurred engraving, and uneven results.
body_text:
¶ How to Adjust the Backlash Parameters
Backlash and scan offset issues can cause misaligned lines, blurred engraving, and uneven results.
This guide explains how to adjust backlash parameters using LightBurn, including preparation,
test file setup, scan offset tuning, and verification to achieve clean, accurate engraving.
¶ Note
The reverse clearance of the equipment has been adjusted to the best engraving effect before leaving the factory.
Please do not adjust it at will unless you encounter special circumstances.
At the same time, the engraving reverse clearance parameters tested by the manufacturer are on the aluminum foil
sheet that comes with the machine, which can be directly filled in.
¶ 1. Preparation
¶ ① Material Preparation
Aluminum foil pieces
Magnifier ×1
One Laser X series device ×1
Computer ×1
¶ ② Debug Software
LightBurn
¶ 2. Adjustment Steps
¶ ① Open the Software
Click Edit → Device Settings to enter the device settings interface.
¶ ② In the Machine Settings Interface
a. Click Basic Settings, check
Enable Scanning Offset Adjustment, and click Add
to add a speed parameter
(set according to personal processing needs)
b. First fill in the speed parameter 600 (according to personal needs).
Do not fill in the offset parameter.
Set Line Shift = 0, then click OK after completing the settings.
¶ 3. Importing Test Files
a. Click File → Import, select the file, and click Open
Note: This test file needs to be provided by the manufacturer’s technical staff.
¶ 4. Set Processing Parameters
a. Double-click the processing parameter status bar to set the engraving parameters.
b. Set:
Engraving speed: 600 mm/s
Line distance (Lines per Inch): 50
After setting, click OK to confirm.
c. Upload the file to the device for processing.
¶ 5. Equipment Processing
a. Place the aluminum foil on the platform, adjust the focal length,
then position and process along the border.
Speed: 600 mm/s
Offset value: 0
b. As shown in the picture, the line offset is particularly obvious
and will affect the actual engraving result.
From top to bottom:
Odd-numbered line segments are used as reference
Even-numbered line segments are biased to the right
You need to increase the offset parameter
to make the lines basically overlap.
¶ 6. Changing the Offset Parameters
a. Follow the above steps to fine-tune the offset parameters between
0.05 – 0.3 mm.
During the adjustment process, continuously observe the engraving effect
to ensure the best setting.
b. After increasing the offset, the lines are roughly aligned,
but the even-numbered line segments are slightly biased to the left.
At this time, slightly reduce the offset
until all lines are basically aligned.
c. Reduce the offset parameter, save, and upload the drawing again.
After adjustment, upload the drawing again for processing.
¶ Result
It can be seen that the odd and even line segments basically overlap,
and the adjustment is completed.

title: Laser Cooling, Temperature & Freeze Safety
excerpt: CO₂ glass tube laser engraving and cutting machines are sensitive to ambient temperature. Low winter temperatures can adversely affect the normal operation of the equipment. Theref
body_text:
¶ Laser Cooling, Temperature, & Freeze Mitigation
¶ Working environment requirements
CO₂ glass tube laser engraving and cutting machines are sensitive to ambient temperature. Low winter temperatures can adversely affect the normal operation of the equipment. Therefore, appropriate protective measures should be taken to ensure stable performance.
To ensure optimal performance of your laser cutting machine year-round, it's crucial to maintain a suitable storage environment. The room temperature should be between 60°F and 80°F (15°C and 27°C), with a humidity level of 40% to 70%. Avoid exposing the machine to direct sunlight.
¶ Cooling System
To ensure optimal performance, the operating environment temperature should be maintained between 15°C and 25°C. Extremely low temperatures can cause the coolant to freeze, affecting heat dissipation and potentially damaging the laser tube. Laser machines typically use either air or water cooling, with the specific cooling method depending on the laser model.
¶ Air Cooling
The 1Laser XRF series of lasers utilizes RF tubes as the laser source and employs an air cooling system for heat dissipation.
Air-cooled tubes utilize fans to circulate air over the tube’s heat sinks, facilitating cooling. The system temperature cannot fall below the ambient room temperature. Freezing is typically not a concern due to the absence of water.
¶ Water Cooling
XT series lasers employ water-cooled glass tubes that are susceptible to sub-freezing temperatures. Optimal system operation requires a water temperature range of 15°C to 25°C. If outdoor temperatures fall below freezing, precautionary measures must be taken to prevent laser tube damage. Note that warranty does not cover freezing-related damage.
The chiller must be filled with distilled water or pure water.
¶ Freeze Mitigation
¶ Provide a constant temperature environment for the workspace
Here are some fundamental ways to protect your water-cooled cooling system from freezing:
Maintain operating temperature: Avoid excessively low operating temperatures. Consider using heating equipment if necessary.
Prevent cold air intrusion: Ensure cold air cannot enter the system. If needed, disconnect the exhaust duct from the outdoor environment.
¶ Drain the coolant
In case of a prolonged power outage in winter or when the equipment is idle for an extended period, it is essential to completely drain the coolant from the chiller and its associated piping.
¶ Add antifreeze Coolant
We use pure distilled water in DC-excited glass water-cooled tubes due to its low conductivity, which allows for the safe passage of 30,000 volts of electricity through the tube. Additives can interfere with this conductivity and potentially damage the cooling system components, particularly over extended periods of use.
🔗 OneLaser Approved Antifreeze
¶ Use a water heater
You can actively warm the water up with a water warmer. Be sure to set the temperature setpoint of warm to below the Chiller’s setpoint by at least 2 Degrees Celsius.

body_text:
¶ How to Fill Water Tanks
To ensure the normal operation of the One Laser XT model, please note that the cold water pump equipped with this device is used to cool the glass tube. The water in the water tank of the water pump has been drained at the factory. If it is powered on directly without adding pure water, it will directly cause electrical failure. Therefore, after receiving the device, please add pure water to the water tank of the water pump as soon as possible to ensure the safe operation of the device.
¶ 1. Preparation
¶ ① Consumable preparation
One Laser XT model device*1, M2 hexagon wrench
¶ ② Debug software
None
¶ 2. Operation step
¶ ① Remove the back cover of the device
Note: The left door of the device needs to be removed at the same time.
Use an M2 hexagonal wrench to remove the hexagonal screws on the back cover and left door of the device and place them together.
Take out the back cover of the device
¶ ② Fill the water tank with pure water
Note: Using pure water as cooling water can prevent scaling and corrosion, improve cooling efficiency, and inhibit the growth of microorganisms, thereby effectively protecting the equipment, ensuring its stable operation and extending its service life.
Find the location of the water tank
Open the water filling cap on the top of the water tank and pour in about 790ml of pure water.
¶ Older models:
Start the equipment, after the pump is started, immediately pour in about 790ml of pure water, observe while pouring, until the water in the storage tank flows into the glass tube.
After has flowed into the tube, you need to add another 150ml or so of pure water, and once you have done so, put the filler cap back on and tighten it.
¶ New model:
The new model of the device in the water tank outside the water level detection, to prevent the device pump dry burning led to damage.
Pour in about 790ml of pure water, start the device and wait for the water to flow in, after flowing into the tube, you need to add another 150ml or so of pure water, after joining, put the water filler cap back on and tighten it.
¶ ③ Antifreeze ratio
Note: To ensure the normal operation of the device in a low temperature environment, when the indoor temperature drops below 10 degrees Celsius, be sure to add antifreeze to the water tank in proportion. If antifreeze is not added, the low temperature may cause abnormalities in the glass tube of the device, thereby affecting the normal operation of the device.
¶ Ratio diagram:
Proportion (Anti-freeze fluid : Distilled water)
Room temperature (Unit: °C)
3:7
-12 ~ -15°C
4:6
-22 ~ -25°C
5:5
-32 ~ -35°C
6:4
-42 ~ -45°C
According to the ratio of pure water and antifreeze shown in the figure above, pour in pure water first, then add antifreeze.
¶ Care Instructions:
The antifreeze fluid will deteriorate to a certain extent when it is used for a long time. After the antifreeze fluid deteriorates, it will be more corrosive and the viscosity will also change, so it needs to be replaced regularly. The frequency of replacement we recommend is to change the water once every 2-3 months (at room temperature). When the ambient temperature starts to rise and the sub-zero temperature is lifted, the circulating cooling water can be replaced with softened water such as distilled water or purified water.
Try to use the same brand of antifreeze. Even if the main components of different types of antifreeze are the same, their additive formulas will be different. It is not advisable to mix them to avoid chemical reactions, precipitation or bubbles.
If laser machine will not be used for a long time, the water inside of laser tube, chiller and water pipes should be drained out, especially for glass laser tube. If buyer did not carry out our instruction, any broken of laser tube caused by this will not be guaranteed.
¶ ④ Post-Processing
After the water tank is filled with water, please reinstall the rear cover and side door of the device.

body_text:
¶ Lifting Lead Screw Fails to Raise the Mirror Mount - Hydra Series
This page explains common reasons why the lifting lead screw fails to raise the mirror mount and provides practical inspection and maintenance steps to restore normal operation. It addresses abnormal noise, stalling during upward movement, and control panel error prompts related to the lifting mechanism.
¶ Problem Description
Initially, there may be a slight noise when the mirror mount moves toward the RF tube position. This noise increases over time with continued use.
The control panel displays a No Extend Device error prompt.
The mirror lifting lead screw moves downward normally (switching from RF to Glass tube), but stutters or stalls when moving upward (switching from Glass to RF tube). Currently, the mirror mount requires a manual upward push to successfully rise.
¶ Cause
The mirror lifting lead screw has not been cleaned or lubricated regularly.
Connections related to the lifting mechanism are loose or disconnected.
The lifting lead screw is slightly bent or misaligned.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Cleaning and Maintenance
Use a cleaning agent, compressed air and high-quality lubricant to clean and maintain the lifting lead screw assembly.
After maintenance, try switching the laser source to see if normal operation is restored.
¶ Method 2. Inspect Wiring
Refer to the wiring diagram below to check all related cables for looseness, disconnection, or physical damage. Ensure all plugs are seated firmly.
¶ Method 3. Check Lead Screw Verticality and Alignment
A bent lead screw will cause resistance at specific points in the travel.
With the power turned off, manually rotate the lifting lead screw to move the mirror mount up and down. Feel for any significant resistance as the mount passes through different positions. If resistance is felt at a specific height, the screw may be bent or out of alignment.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Random stray lines during laser processing - X Series
excerpt: This page explains why random stray lines may appear during laser processing, even when they are not present in the original design file. It provides a detailed breakdown of common
body_text:
¶ Random Stray Lines Appearing During Processing - X Series
This page explains why random stray lines may appear during laser processing, even when they are not present in the original design file. It provides a detailed breakdown of common causes—ranging from data transmission errors to hardware failures—and step-by-step solutions to help restore stable and accurate machine operation.
¶ Problem Description
A file that previously ran normally now causes the laser head to move randomly along the X or Y axis, leaving random stray lines that do not exist in the original design. In some cases, the laser head may even continuously crash into the X-axis or Y-axis limit switches during operation.
Source: Image provided by a customer
¶ Cause
Clicking Start directly in LightBurn can cause errors if the data stream is interrupted.
If the computer is running on high memory, data packets sent to the machine may be lost.
Damaged switches may send false triggers.
Loose, burnt, or damaged plugs on the X/Y drivers, or loose connections at the motor ends.
Internal damage to the X or Y axis motors.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Send Files to the Machine
Problems caused by clicking Start directly in LightBurn are almost always due to an unstable live transmission.
Instead of Start, click Send in LightBurn to transfer the file completely to the machine’s internal memory. Then, initiate the job directly from the machine's control panel.
¶ Method 2. Clear Computer Memory
Computers can accumulate a large amount of cache after long periods of operation, which may interfere with data processing.
Restart your computer to release memory and clear the cache. After rebooting, try sending the file and running the job again.
¶ Method 3. Inspect Limit Switches
Open the Diagnose page on the controller panel. Manually press the limit switch with your finger.
Check if the corresponding indicator on the Diagnose page changes from green to red.
If the color changes: The switch is functioning correctly.
If the color remains unchanged: The limit switch is damaged and needs replacement.
¶ Method 4. Inspect the X-Axis or Y-Axis Driver
Disconnect the power. Unscrew the screws on the right side of the XRF and remove the right side cover.
Locate the X-axis/Y-axis driver (near the back end of the machine) and check for any loose or burned connections at the driver plug:
If the plug is loose: Push the plug in tightly, ensuring a secure connection. Then, try moving the X-axis or Y-axis.
If the plug is burned: Take photos and contact customer service via ZOHO to request a replacement for the damaged driver plug (if the machine is still under warranty).
Prepare a multimeter and set it to continuity mode. Turn the machine OFF and unplug the wires from the driver.
Use the multimeter probes to check continuity on:
① Black and Yellow & Green wires
② Brown and Blue wires
The multimeter should beep or display "0L" to confirm continuity.
The diagram below illustrates checking the Y-axis driver as an example.
¶ Method 5. Inspect the X-Axis or Y-Axis Motor
Locate the X-axis motor and verify the wire plug is securely connected.
Open the cover at the back of the honeycomb board to locate the Y-axis motor. Check if the wire plug is connected and if the motor is functioning.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

excerpt: The automatic focusing method uses contact-based focusing. Soft materials may affect the focusing accuracy (e.g., sponge, leather). For soft materials, please use manual focusing.
body_text:
¶ How to Focus
¶ Introduction
The automatic focusing method uses contact-based focusing. Soft materials may affect the focusing accuracy (e.g., sponge, leather). For soft materials, please use manual focusing.
You can use 6mm acrylic to make a focusing ruler
¶ Manual Focusing
Manual focusing is ideal for materials that may compress, bend, or warp under pressure. Follow the steps below for accurate results:
¶ 1. Position the Material
Place the material on the honeycomb table, ensure it is flat, and secure it to prevent movement.
¶ 2. Place the Focusing Ruler
Slide your 6mm acrylic focusing ruler directly underneath the laser head.
This sets the correct focusing distance between the nozzle and work surface.
¶ 3. Adjust the Platform Height
Use the machine’s height adjustment control to raise or lower the platform until the laser head just lightly touches the focusing ruler.
Once the head makes contact, the focus is set.
¶ Automatic Focusing
Automatic focus is fast and convenient for most materials, especially hard, flat surfaces.
¶ 1. Position the Material
Place the material securely on the honeycomb table and move the laser head above it.
¶ 2. Initiate Auto Focus
On the touchscreen, select “Focus” → then tap “OK”.
The machine will lower itself until the contact sensor reaches the correct height.
¶ ⚠️ Important Note
When using automatic focus, the material must be placed on the table.
Running auto-focus without material underneath can cause the sensor to overtravel, potentially damaging the laser head or table.

title: Hydra Dual-Source Laser: Features & Advantages
excerpt: This page provides a clear overview of how dual-source laser systems combine the strengths of RF tubes and glass tubes to deliver superior cutting and engraving performance. You’ll
body_text:
¶ Introduction to Dual-Source Features and Advantages
This page provides a clear overview of how dual-source laser systems combine the strengths of RF tubes and glass tubes to deliver superior cutting and engraving performance. You’ll learn how each tube type contributes to precision, power, efficiency, and material versatility—making dual-source machines an ideal solution for diverse production needs.
¶ Preface
In the field of non-metal material processing, the dual-source laser cutting machine has become an ideal choice for many enterprises due to its unique design and outstanding performance. It cleverly combines the advantages of RF tubes and glass tubes, meeting a wide range of processing needs and significantly improving processing efficiency and economic benefits.
¶ Complementary Advantages of RF and Glass Tubes
RF Tube
The RF tube can produce high-quality beams and fine spots, making it suitable for precision processing. Whether it's intricate pattern engraving or high-quality edge cutting of materials, the RF tube can perfectly reproduce details, making it ideal for crafting fine arts and electronic components.
Glass Tube
The glass tube boasts higher power and stronger penetration, excelling at quickly completing large-area cutting tasks. Although its cutting quality is slightly inferior to that of the RF tube, it is sufficient for basic needs and has certain advantages when cutting thicker materials.
Flexibility in Handling Different Material Thicknesses
For thin material processing, such as fabrics and leather, the fine spot of the RF tube can prevent excessive cutting damage, ensuring the quality of the finished product. For cutting thick materials like thick acrylic boards and bamboo or wood products, the high power and penetration of the glass tube can easily handle the task, meeting basic cutting requirements.
Power Control and Processing Precision
The RF tube has excellent power control precision, capable of low-power output, which meets the needs of precision engraving and other fine processing tasks. In contrast, the glass tube cannot output low power, making it unsuitable for processing tasks that require high precision in power control, which can lead to substandard processing quality.
¶ Enhancing Processing Efficiency and Economic Benefits
Reducing Equipment Costs
Compared to purchasing two different types of laser cutting machines, the dual-source cutting machine has a lower equipment cost. Enterprises do not need to buy separate machines for different processing needs, saving a significant amount of investment. This also reduces the space occupied by equipment, allowing for more efficient use of production areas.
Reducing Equipment Switching
During the processing, the dual-source cutting machine can quickly switch light sources on the same machine, greatly reducing the time and labor intensity of equipment switching, and improving production efficiency. It also minimizes the risk of errors caused by equipment switching, ensuring the stability and reliability of the processing process.
Increasing Processing Speed
By reasonably allocating light source usage according to processing needs, such as using the RF tube for precision areas and the glass tube for large areas or low-precision areas, the machine can maximize processing speed while ensuring quality, meeting the high demands of enterprises for production efficiency.

body_text:
¶ Poor Processing Effect in Laser Cutting - X Series
Poor Processing Effect is a troubleshooting guide that helps users identify and resolve issues where laser cutting fails to cut through the material. This page explains the most common causes—from material conditions to optical path alignment—and provides practical inspection and adjustment steps to restore proper cutting performance.
¶ Problem Description
During laser cutting, the material cannot be cut through, even though the job appears to run normally.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Material issues
The material surface is uneven, coated or has impurities that will affect the cutting effect.
Make sure the material surface is clean and flat, and pre-treat it if necessary.
¶ Method 2. The reflector or focusing mirror is completely damaged
Failure to maintain the equipment on time may result in the reflector or focusing lens not being able to transmit or reflect light. Check whether the light path reflector and lens have good light transmittance.
¶ Method 3. Laser optical path deviation
The laser light path is offset, which will cause the laser to hit the inside of the laser head or the inside of the device, and the light cannot be emitted.
Please use double-sided tape to stick on the three-mirror frame, and press the point shooting to check whether the light spots of the five light source points in the platform overlap.
If there is an offset, please refer to the “How to adjust the laser light path”.
¶ Method 4. Incorrect focus adjustment
The bending of the material itself and the inconsistent height of the working area will cause different focal lengths at different positions in the cutting area, especially when cutting large-format patterns.
Please use a strong magnet to flatten the material and use a focusing ruler to check whether the height of each area of the working platform is consistent.
If it is not accurate, please use the focusing ruler to readjust the focal length.
¶ Method 5. Laser is weak or damaged
The laser life has reached its limit, resulting in a decrease in light output power.
The laser life is usually between 2500–4000 hours, and the specific life depends on the actual operating conditions.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

¶ Problem Description

¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. IP setting error
After the device is connected to the network cable, please check whether the computer local IP, software IP, and device IP are in the same network segment.
If they are inconsistent, please set the first 3 digits of the IP segment to be consistent.
¶ Method 2. Network cable is damaged
Use a network cable tester to test whether the network cable is damaged.
Determine whether the network cable is damaged according to the indicator lights on the network cable tester. Turn on the switch, and the indicator lights on the main tester and the remote test end should flash from 1 to 8 in sequence. If the indicator lights flash in sequence, it means that the straight-through network cable has good connectivity. If they do not flash in sequence, it means that the network cable is not connected and needs to be replaced.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: How to Adjust the Laser Light Path
excerpt: This guide explains how to adjust the laser light path on the OneLaser X Series safely and correctly. It covers critical precautions, required tools, and preparation steps to help
body_text:
¶ How to Adjust the Laser Light Path
This guide explains how to adjust the laser light path on the OneLaser X Series safely and correctly. It covers critical precautions, required tools, and preparation steps to help ensure accurate alignment while preventing unnecessary damage or time-consuming recalibration.
¶ Note:
When the device leaves the factory, the optical path has been precisely adjusted to the best state.
If you are not sure whether the optical path of the device has shifted, please do not adjust the optical path lens knob or locking screw at will.
Once the optical path locking screw or knob is adjusted, the optical path of the device may shift.
If it shifts, you may need at least 4 hours to readjust the optical path of the device.
¶ 1. Preparation
¶ ① Material preparation
Double-sided tape × 1
10mm Acrylic × 1
Flathead screwdriver × 1
M3 Hexagon wrench × 1
M2.5 Hexagon wrench × 1
M2 Hexagon wrench × 1
One Laser X series × 1
¶ ② Disassembling the Case
¶ A. Removing the back cover
Use an M2 hexagon wrench and carefully remove the screws according to the instructions in the picture, and place them in a unified manner.
¶ B. Removing the front cover
Use an M2 hexagon wrench and carefully remove the screws according to the instructions in the picture, and place them in a unified manner.
¶ C. Removing the side door
Use an M2 hexagon wrench and carefully remove the screws according to the instructions in the picture, and place them in a unified manner.
¶ ③ Set panel parameters
¶ A. Set the burst parameters
a. Click on the menu → Laser setting → Setting parameters
b. Set the burst mode to continuous, the time to 5 ms, and the power to 30%.
¶ 2. Adjustment steps
¶ Note:
Please stick the double-sided tape on the front of the frame to be adjusted, then move the laser head and lightly press the shot button to adjust the optical path.
During this process, please carefully observe the changes in the optical path.
¶ ① Adjust the light path from one reflection to two reflections
Stick the double-sided tape to the front of the second mirror frame.
That is, adjust the light source points ① and ③ as shown in the figure below to coincide with each other.
¶ A. Adjust the overlap of ① and ③ light spots
When a large deviation occurs, such as the following:
¶ a. Large offset adjustment
At this moment, the light spot is offset to a large extent, and it is necessary to adjust the bottom bracket to make the light spots roughly overlap.
After loosening the fixing screws of the black bracket, start adjusting the upper reflective frame.
During the adjustment process:
Fix the screws while fine-tuning the frame
Ensure the light spots roughly overlap
After tightening the screws on one side, check if there is any deviation
Observe the direction of movement of the light spot when tightening
Push the frame in the opposite direction accordingly
Fix the frame until the lenses roughly overlap
¶ The light spots roughly overlap:
¶ b. Adjust lens distance
Tighten the three gold nuts on the outside of the lens and the lens will move back, ensuring there is about 1 cm gap between the lens and the frame.
If the distance between the lenses is about 1 cm, there is no need to tighten the nut again.
¶ c. Loosen frame nut
Use an M2.5 hexagon wrench to loosen the silver-white nut of the frame.
¶ d. Adjustment Instructions
In the figure:
When screw No. 1 is rotated clockwise, the light source will move downward
When screw No. 2 is rotated clockwise, the light source will move to the right
When screw No. 3 is rotated clockwise, the light source will move to the upper left
(Counterclockwise rotation will move the light source in the opposite direction.)
After each fine-tuning of the screw, please slightly tighten the silver-white nut to prevent the light source from shifting a second time.
Adjust these three screws until the front and rear light sources coincide at the same point.
¶ 3. Adjust the Optical Path from the Second Reflector to the Third Reflector
Stick double-sided tape to the front of the three-mirror frame.
This step adjusts the light source points ①, ②, ③, and ④ so they overlap and are positioned at the center point.
¶ A. Adjust ① and ② Light Source Points to Basically Coincide
a. Use an M2.5 hexagonal wrench to loosen the two fixing screws of the second mirror frame.
b. Move the frame:
Gently move the second mirror frame, move the laser head back and forth, and press the point shooting button to let the laser hit light source points ① and ②.
After the front and rear light spots appear on the third mirror frame, fix one screw and gently swing the second mirror frame to make light source points ① and ② basically overlap.
After overlap, tighten the screw.
¶ B. Adjust the Overlap of Light Source Points ①, ②, ③, and ④
a. Use an M2.5 hexagonal wrench to loosen the two silver nuts on the frame.
b. Adjustment Instructions:
When screw No. 1 rotates clockwise, the light source moves downward
When screw No. 2 rotates clockwise, the light source moves to the right
When screw No. 3 rotates clockwise, the light source moves to the upper left
Counterclockwise rotation moves the light source in the opposite direction
After each fine-tuning of the screw, slightly tighten the silver-white nut to prevent the light source from shifting again.
Adjust these three screws until ①, ②, ③, and ④ light sources overlap.
¶ C. Adjust ①, ②, ③, ④ Light Source Points to the Center Point
a. When there is a left-right deviation from the center point, adjust it by adjusting the two-mirror frame
Use an M2.5 hexagonal wrench to loosen the two silver nuts.
Gently push the second mirror frame:
If biased to the left, move it to the right
If biased to the right, move it to the left
Adjust until the light source is centered.
b. Height deviation adjustment
When there is a height deviation from the center point, the laser height needs to be adjusted.
i. Use an M2.5 hexagonal wrench to loosen the two jacking bolts on the laser base.
RF Tube:
Turn the knob clockwise to raise the laser tube, counterclockwise to lower it.
Glass Tube:
Adjust in the same way and tighten the bottom jacking bolt after adjustment.
Note:
The front and rear heights of the laser must remain consistent, and the top screws on both sides must be tightened.
¶ D. Adjust Verticality
Set the burst power to 60% and burst through 10 × 10 mm acrylic.
Visually check whether the cutting result is vertical.
If the verticality leans to the left, raise the laser
If the verticality leans to the right, lower the laser
¶ 4. Next Steps
After completing the adjustment:
Ensure all fixing screws are fully tightened
Reinstall all door covers
Tighten all screws securely

¶ Touchscreen get stucked after turning on - X Series

After turning the machine on, the touch screen panel has been stuck in this page and cannot enter the main interface.

Emergency stop switch power cable
Touchscreen signal cable
PM2.5 detector power cable
Reseat the connector between the panel and the control board.
¶ Method 3. Control board or touchscreen panel fault
If the issue persists after trying the above methods, please replace the component with a new one for testing.
¶ Method 4. Incorrect firmware version installed
Remove the right-side panel of the machine and inspect the label on the motherboard. Ensure that the motherboard and HMI firmware updated files you downloaded exactly match the version indicated on the label.

¶ Wifi cannot connect - X Series
This page provides a step-by-step troubleshooting guide for resolving Wi-Fi connection issues when the machine operates normally but cannot establish a wireless connection. It explains common configuration errors, connection mistakes, and hardware checks to help restore stable Wi-Fi communication.
¶ Problem Description
Note: To ensure file transfer efficiency and stability, please avoid transmitting data via Wi-Fi through thick walls or heavy obstructions.
The machine is operating normally, but a Wi-Fi connection cannot be established.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Incorrect Switch Module Settings
An incorrect channel setting on the internal switch module will prevent the Wi-Fi from connecting.
Use a 2 mm Hex Wrench to remove the 6 screws from the right-side door of the machine and locate the switch module.
Ensure that Button 1 is pressed down. Button 1 activates Channel 1 (Wi-Fi Mode), which allows the computer to connect to the machine's Wi-Fi hotspot.
¶ Method 2. Incorrect Wi-Fi Connection
Please verify that you are connecting to the correct network:
Direct Connection: If you are connecting to the machine’s local hotspot, verify the name follows the format: Machine Model + Hotspot + Last 5 digits of Serial Number.
Bridged Connection: If you have bridged the machine to an upstream router, ensure your computer is connected to that same Wi-Fi.
Connecting Guide: Connect XT&XRF to LightBurn via WiFi
¶ Method 3. Inspect the Wi-Fi Receiver and Components
Check for hardware damage or loose connections:
Check if the green indicator light on the Wi-Fi module is illuminated. If it is off, verify that the power supply is functional and the network cable is properly plugged into the controller board.
Ensure the network cable is securely seated in its port.
Ensure the power supply wire for the module is tightly connected.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

¶ LightBurn Software Introduction
¶ What Is LightBurn Software?
LightBurn is professional laser control software that allows you to design, edit, and send jobs directly to your laser machine. It combines design tools with machine control, making it suitable for both beginners and advanced users.
With LightBurn, you can:
Design vector graphics and layouts
Adjust laser parameters such as power and speed
Preview jobs before running
Send files directly to the laser cutter
LightBurn is widely used across hobby, business, and industrial laser workflows.
¶ How the License Works
A LightBurn license is a digital key used to unlock the software for permanent use.
Every new license comes with a year of free updates from the date you first activate it. After a year, you'll still be able to use any version of LightBurn released before your license expired, but you'll need to renew your key in order to continue receiving updates for another year. If you renew before your key expires, you'll receive an additional two months on your one-year renewal.
A LightBurn license automatically comes with 3 seats, meaning you can activate it on three computers at one time. You can use the LightBurn License Portal to view and remove activations on your key, freeing up activations in use on old or inoperable computers so you can activate on new ones.

During the operation of the device, no red dot indication is found.

Find the energy-saving control panel shown below. Remove the wires as indicated, then use a multimeter set to DC 5V to measure the output voltage.
Normal voltage: If the voltage is 5V, the red light indicator is faulty. Please contact OneLaser support for replacement.
Abnormal voltage: If the voltage is not 5V, the TL energy-saving control motherboard is faulty. Please contact OneLaser support for replacement.

title: One Laser Touchscreen Alarm Guide (X Series - XRF/ XT)
excerpt: The machine will issue an “out-of-bounds” alarm when the design file extends beyond the physical working limits of the device. For example, the X Series model provides a processing
body_text:
This article provides an overview of common alarm messages that may appear on the One Laser touchscreen interface. These alerts are designed to protect the machine, ensure operational stability, and assist users in identifying potential risks during laser processing. Because the device firmware is continually updated, users may occasionally encounter pop-up messages not yet included in this guide.
¶ 1. X- or Y-Axis Boundary Exceeded
¶ Overview
The machine will issue an “out-of-bounds” alarm when the design file extends beyond the physical working limits of the device. For example, the X Series model provides a processing area of 600 × 300 mm. When either axis exceeds this range, the system interrupts job execution to prevent mechanical collision or excessive travel.
¶ Why This Happens
This alert commonly arises from:
A design file larger than the available workspace
Incorrect origin selection that shifts the design outside the valid working area
Misalignment caused by offsetting the starting point too close to an edge
In the reference diagram provided with the machine,the yellow region represents the machine’s working boundary,the green square indicates the user-defined origin,and the blue/gray areas denote the file’s placement.
If the origin is selected incorrectly—such as the example where it is set near the edge—the file may partially fall outside the allowable range, triggering the alarm.
¶ Recommended Actions
Verify that the design dimensions fall within the permitted workspace.
Reset the origin and ensure that the entire file lies safely within the machine’s processing area.
¶ 2. Insufficient Buffer Distance
¶ Overview
During engraving, the laser head requires a certain amount of buffer space to accelerate, decelerate, and execute rapid directional changes. If the file is positioned too close to the boundary of the working area, the machine may detect insufficient buffer distance and trigger a warning.
¶ Why This Happens
This alert is typically caused by:
A file placed extremely close to the workspace edges
An origin location that does not leave the head enough space for motion planning
¶ Recommended Actions
Adjust the origin to give the design additional margin from the machine’s physical limits.
Re-run the job once sufficient buffer distance has been ensured.
¶ 3. Water Protection Trigger (XT Series)
¶ Overview
The XT Series utilizes a glass CO₂ laser tube paired with a water-cooling system. To protect the tube from overheating, the machine incorporates a water-flow sensor. When this sensor fails to detect water movement at the beginning of a job, the system displays a water-protection alarm. This prevents tube damage and ensures long-term operational safety.
¶ Inspection Point
To access the water-cooling components, open the rear housing using an M2 screwdriver.
¶ Recommended Actions
Confirm that the water pump’s signal cable is properly connected.
Check whether the water pump is operating normally and providing consistent flow.
¶ 4. Combined Alarm Window
¶ (Door Cover Protection / Flame Alarm / Water Temperature Alarm)
Several safety-related alerts share a common pop-up interface. When this window appears, users should assess the possible causes one by one.
¶ 4.1 Door Cover Protection
¶ Overview
For safety reasons, the device requires all doors and covers to remain fully closed during operation. If any cover is open or not securely latched, the system issues a door-protection alarm and stops the job.
Recommended Action:
Ensure that all covers and access panels are completely closed before restarting the process.
¶ 4.2 Water Temperature Alarm
¶ Overview
When the water temperature inside the cooling tank exceeds 45 °C, the machine automatically halts operation and emits a beeping sound. This prevents thermal damage to the laser tube, which is sensitive to elevated temperatures.
Recommended Action:
Wait until the water temperature falls back to a safe range before resuming work.
¶ 4.3 Flame Alarm
¶ Overview
The system includes a flame-detection sensor that monitors for abnormal combustion events within the workspace. If the sensor detects a flame or receives an irregular signal, the machine will stop immediately for safety.
¶ Diagnostic Steps
Inspect the flame-detection probe to ensure it is not bent or obstructed, and verify that all wiring is intact.
Open the right-side panel (remove the cover with a screwdriver).
Locate the intelligent control board and disconnect the IN6 interface.
Restart the machine:
If the beeping alarm persists even after IN6 is disconnected, the control board may have malfunctioned and should be evaluated by technical support.

body_text:
¶ How to Adjust the Air Pipe Screw
This guide explains how to properly adjust the air pipe securing screw on X-series laser machines. It outlines when adjustment is necessary, required tools, and step-by-step instructions to restore airflow while preventing damage to the air pipe.
¶ Caution
The screw securing the air pipe is calibrated to its optimal state before leaving the factory.
Do not tighten it unnecessarily, as this may crush the pipe and cut off the airflow.
Only adjust this screw if there is no airflow during processing.
¶ Preparation
X-series machine
M2 hex wrench
Flat-head screwdriver
¶ Operation
¶ Remove the Laser Head Covers
You will need to remove both the front and right-side covers of the laser head.
Front Cover: The front cover is magnetic; pull it off directly.
Right-Side Cover: Use the 2 mm hex wrench to remove the securing screws.
¶ Adjust the Air Pipe Securing Screw
Locate the air pipe adjustment screw as shown below.
Use a flat-head screwdriver to perform the adjustment:
Clockwise: Tightens the screw.
Counter-clockwise: Loosens the screw.
IMPORTANT: If the screw is too loose, it may fall out during operation.
If it is too tight, airflow may be restricted or completely blocked.
Adjust until the pipe is secure while maintaining proper airflow.
¶ Reassembly
Once the adjustment is complete, reinstall the right-side cover with the screws
and snap the magnetic front cover back into place.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a
support ticket.
A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis.

title: Axis Driver Red Flashing Light Error - X Series
excerpt: This page explains how to diagnose and resolve issues when an axis driver indicator light turns red and flashes. It covers what the flashing patterns mean, why the driver enters pr
body_text:
¶ Axis Driver Indicator Light is Red and Flashing - X Series
This page explains how to diagnose and resolve issues when an axis driver indicator light turns red and flashes. It covers what the flashing patterns mean, why the driver enters protection mode, and how to safely restore normal machine operation.
¶ Problem Description
Remove the right-side cover panel to locate the axis drivers. Under normal operating conditions, the status indicator light on the driver should be solid green. If the red indicator light begins to flash, it indicates an abnormality with the driver or motor position.
¶ Cause&Solution
Please refer to the table for the corresponding questions and solutions.
Red Light Flashes
Protection Function
Cause
Solution
1 Flash
Overcurrent / Short Circuit
A short circuit or wiring error has occurred in the motor or driver, triggering overcurrent protection.
Power off the equipment, inspect the motor wiring for the corresponding axis, and then power the equipment back on.
2 Flashes
Overvoltage Protection
The driver enters protection mode when the voltage exceeds 40 V DC.
Power the equipment off and then back on. If this occurs frequently, consider slightly reducing the input power supply voltage.
4 Flashes
Phase Loss Protection
The driver was powered on without a motor connected, or there is a current imbalance, excessive current, or motor coil overheating.
Power off the equipment, inspect the motor wiring for the corresponding axis, replug the connectors, and power back on.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: How to Apply and Fine-tune Your Scanning Offset Settings - X Series
excerpt: Engraving result in blurry effects or "ghosting" (double images).
body_text:
¶ How to Apply and Fine-Tune Your Scanning Offset Settings - X Series
¶ Problem Description
Engraving result in blurry effects or "ghosting" (double images).
¶ Cause
The Scanning Offset parameters tested at the factory were not written to the machine from LightBurn after the machine was received.
Vibrations during shipping and logistics may have caused a slight deviation.
¶ Solution
Every machine is shipped from the factory with a dedicated Scanning Offset Settings parameter card (as shown in the image below).
After connecting your computer to the machine, open Device Settings and click Basic Settings to find the Scanning Offset Adjust. Enter the values from your parameter card.
Important Reminders:
The values on the card are in mm/s. Using other units, such as inch/s, will lead to incorrect Scanning Offset results. Ensure that your software is set to the correct unit: mm/s.
Click Write and then click Read to confirm that the parameters have been successfully stored in the machine.
Before closing the window, ensure that Scanning Offset Adjustment is enabled.
For dual-source machines, you must enter the specific parameters for both Laser1 and Laser2 separately.
Due to vibrations during shipping and transport, the factory-set parameters may become slightly misaligned. We recommend validating the precision by performing a test engraving after entering the initial parameters:
Draw a rectangle on your workspace. Set the Layer Mode to Fill.
Double-click the layer to enter the settings window. Set the Speed to a corresponding value from your parameter card (e.g., 400 mm/s, 800 mm/s, or 1200 mm/s) and apply an appropriate Power setting. Set the Line Interval to 0.5 mm.
Observe the test result, as shown in the image below.
If the ends of the even-numbered scan lines finish further to the right than the odd-numbered lines, you should slightly increase the Line Shift value.
If the even-numbered lines finish further to the left, you should slightly decrease the Line Shift value.
Note:
The adjustment range is very small, typically from 0.001 to 0.01 (e.g., changing 0.150 to 0.155). You may need to repeatedly test and adjust until the ends of the even-numbered and odd-numbered scan lines are perfectly aligned.
Once the adjustment is complete, you can Export and save the Scanning Offset Settings file. This allows you to directly Import the configured parameter file if you ever connect a new computer to this machine for processing.
Important Reminder:
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

title: Z-Axis Stuttering & Abnormal Noise Fix - Hydra Series
excerpt: This page provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for resolving stuttering, abnormal noise, or jamming issues when the Z-axis platform moves up or down. It outlines common s
body_text:
¶ Stuttering and Abnormal Noise When Moving Platform (Z-Axis) - Hydra Series
This page provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for resolving stuttering, abnormal noise, or jamming issues when the Z-axis platform moves up or down. It outlines common symptoms, root causes, and step-by-step corrective actions to restore normal Z-axis operation.
¶ Problem Description
Stuttering or abnormal noise occurs when moving the Z-axis up or down.
The platform stalls at a specific height and cannot move further upward.
Physical resistance or strange sounds are noticed when manually pulling the Z-axis belt.
¶ Cause
Alignment Issues: One of the Z-axis lead screws is not perfectly vertical or parallel.
Driver Settings: Incorrect DIP switch positions on the Z-axis driver.
Parameter Errors: Incorrect factory parameter settings in the software.
¶ Solution
¶ Method 1. Inspect and Align the Z-Axis Lead Screws
This issue typically occurs in new machines or after a significant physical impact that causes the lead screws to bend or shift out of vertical alignment.
Open the front bottom door panel and check the four lead screws for any visible bending.
To ensure the lead screws are parallel, measure the distance between the lead screws as shown in the diagram (Sides A, B, and C).
To measure Side B, you must first remove the metal protective plate.
The lengths of sides with the same color (e.g. all A sides, all B sides, all C sides) should be identical. It is normal for Sides B and Sides C to have different values.
Measure from the edge of one lead screw base to the edge of the opposite lead screw base.
If you find a side with an inconsistent length, loosen the two screws on the black base, slightly adjust the position until the measurements match, and then retighten the screws.
¶ Method 2. Check the Z-Axis Driver DIP Switches
Open the bottom door panel on the right side of the machine.
Locate the Z-axis driver (usually positioned toward the top left).
Ensure that only switches 2, 3, and 7 are in the ON (pressed down) position. All other switches must be in the OFF position.
¶ Method 3. Verify Factory Parameters
Open LightBurn and navigate to Machine Settings. Then locate the Z Axis Settings section.
Check if your parameters match the standard values (see reference image). If the values do not match, please contact the OneLaser after-sales team to obtain the correct parameter values.
